Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, cops allegedly found three firearms, three magazines, and sixteen bullets. but Rod’s lawyers want a judge to order that evidence thrown out as so-called "fruit of the poisonous tree" from the unconstitutional search.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as we’ve reported. Rod was arrested about a month after the alleged burglary took place. He was booked on 14 charges, including aggravated assault involving the use of a firearm.

Sebagaimana diketahui, police say he and one of his associates got into a verbal argument as they were carrying out items from the residence. which is when a Glock 20 10mm semi-automatic pistol was pulled and fired.

Instead, she gets Martti: a balding, beer-bellied 49-year-old bloodsucker who slips into a Santa suit to gain entry to homes and devour entire families. Sold by Charades and produced by Bufo, Allfilm and Hobab, “Red Snow” debuts exclusive clip here:.

Mixing vampire mythology with Santa Claus – “and the sexual undertones that come with it” – has surprised some viewers, admitted Rautsi.

Berdasarkan laporan, “it can be disturbing to people, but it’s not a disturbing film. That’s the part of its charm: the grotesque and all the twists and turns in the story. It’s set in this absurd, outrageous world that hopefully allows me to get away with it. ”.

It was important to still ground the film in some “recognizable emotion,” stated Rautsi.

Berdasarkan laporan, “these are heightened characters, but there are also some glimmers of what they are actually going through. We don’t necessarily have to root for them all the time, but we’re along for the ride – despite all the madness. ”.

Christmas can be a stressful time, with or without vampires.

Berdasarkan laporan, “for me, this juicy christmas setting acts as a boiling kettle. We’ve all been there. We know the feeling of spending Christmas with family when you’re supposed to be jolly but it’s actually miserable,” he laughed.

Diungkapkan bahwa “you can see this in all of shane black’s films that are set at christmas but not about christmas. I think they have affected me, too. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, rautsi doesn’t hide his affection for horror. Known for shorts “Helsinki Mansplaining Massacre” and “The Night of the Living Dicks,” he has also written “Nightborn” and “Hatching. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i’m a nervous person. to be afraid. But then we go and see a horror film, and we celebrate the fact that it’s O. K. Fear is such a taboo subject – people don’t talk about it. A good horror film is my comfort zone, though, because it validates the internal life of someone who’s afraid. It can be fun to experience it in a safe setting,” he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, despite its wild premise, “red snow” captures how he perceives life. It can be scary, but it can also make you laugh.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i’m constantly laughing about all the things i’m afraid of. The goal of the film was to express how I experience things. You can be going through something ridiculous and then notice something beautiful about the whole situation. Life can be so many things, all at once, within the space of five seconds. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the o2 opened in north greenwich, london in 2007 utilizing the existing space of the millennium dome. It originally housed the Millennium Experience in 2000, but suffered from low attendance and eventually closed the following year.

In 2003, construction began on a new 20,000-capacity arena within the dome, bringing a new indoor arena to the English capital and exceeding Wembley Arena’s 12,500 capacity.

Diungkapkan bahwa the venue launched in 2007 and has played host to a number of music’s biggest artists. Diungkapkan bahwa the o2 is owned and operated by aeg international. THR can now exclusively premiere a clip from One Sweet Hour.

O’Byrne and Recks talked to THR about the collaborative atmosphere on the set of One Sweet Hour, how its upcoming premiere means additional emotions for them following the sudden death of Lydon and what audiences can take away from the road movie – well, boat movie, to be precise.

Diungkapkan bahwa the boat idea actually came from an experience that writer o’brien had. “He had done a documentary where he was himself on a boat, about 10, 15 years ago. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the two had also previously discussed an elvis idea. “We had this character, an Elvis impersonator, that we tried to get into a film years back, and the story didn’t work,” the director tells THR. “But the character had been hanging around. So we decided to put Elvis on the boat. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, giving him an estranged brother was no huge leap of faith, given that o’brien has written a lot of stories about family. “So, we [figured] we would put the two of them in this confined space on a very slow road trip and see what comes out of it,” Recks says.

Diungkapkan bahwa did o’byrne come on board, literally, as a man of god due to his conclave experience, you may wonder. And I worked with Gary just really briefly over the years, but I knew him for about 30 years. I knew Eugene just tangentially, and I’ve been a fan of his work. “They gave me a call, and I had known Gary and Eugene. And it all happened pretty quickly. I had not met Declan before. “At least, it wasn’t a priest in this one, so it was a different branch of the clergy,” the actor jokes. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the stars, the director and the writer spent some time together working on the script and the characters in advance of the shoot. “And because we had worked only a very small amount with each other, Gary and I got a chance to get to know each other, and that was really lovely. “We are older, and none of us was trying to prove anything. Sebagaimana diketahui, concludes the actor: “it became zen filmmaking in a way, in that we were on the boat, and it just moved along at that slow pace. You can’t just turn it around. So there was a built-in pause in the whole thing, and we were blessed with really glorious weather. And when we had to do a second take, everyone had to sit, and the boat had to move slowly, slowly back. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, adds recks: “you are only allowed 15 people on the boat, so we were in our own little world for the 10 days that we were on it. It was lovely, and it just meant that it was a very small, tight-knit bunch on the boat, and it just didn’t feel rushed at any time. We were left alone, left to our own devices. It was just two actors and the rest was crew, and that was it. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, lydon’s death at the end of april is still on his creative partners’ minds. “It was a terrible shock,” says Decks. “The only consolation for us was that we all felt Gary had such a good time while making the film. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, o’byrne echoes the feeling of shock and sadness. “His sons, his brothers and his partner all came forward and said, ‘This was one of the happiest experiences Gary’s ever had. It was just beautiful. I think any of us involved in it would look back say [the same]. And I think for family and friends of Gary and us all, it means a lot that we got to share a really lovely experience with him and that he was so genuinely pleased with the whole experience. “There is just an extra weight to the film now for us who participated in it,” he shares. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one sweet hour is a bittersweet film. But if this is his last film, it’s an extraordinary one. “And in a way, it’s an ode to Gary. There is another film that he did afterwards. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, lydon’s gerry lights up when he performs as elvis. I knew he could sing. But he absolutely threw himself into it, and I agree – I don’t think you’d know from looking at it that he was terrified. We had to push him a little bit. And we got him a movement coach. “He was absolutely terrified. The star must have really enjoyed those scenes then. Well, actually… “It’s funny – that was the thing he was most worried about,” shares Decks. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but going back to how gerry feels very different when he is on stage, that’s where the title one sweet hour comes into play. “He gets up on the stage, he puts on this costume and he puts on a mask. And for that time that he’s up on the stage, everything else is gone – all that matters is the music. “It’s his opportunity to escape the trauma that he’s carrying,” explains Recks. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, o’byrne’s colum handles the trauma differently. “He becomes silent and just anonymous and searches for a spiritual way out without ever dealing with it. “He literally puts on a costume as well, but he does the opposite,” he tells THR. So neither of them has ever dealt with what happened. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the creative team knows that the themes explored in one sweet hour will be recognizable to people in ireland and beyond. “But we didn’t want to make a very heavy film. “Everyone knows somebody who’s had trauma within their family, but in Ireland, we’ve also had trauma brought on us by the church and by the state,” Decks says. Tonally, we wanted people to engage with the characters and go on a journey with them. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, o’byrne also highlights a key social takeaway. “The film said to me that unless we talk about stuff, we can’t get over things,” he says. No one can bury stuff. We fool ourselves if we bury ourselves and isolate. And in the end, Gerry gets to make a connection. ”.

A connection with whom, you ask? Well, you have to see One Sweet Hour and go on that journey through central Ireland with Gerry and Colum to find out.

#12. SAG-AFTRA Boss Says AI Takedowns Matter More Than Damages To Performers

SAG-AFTRA Boss Says AI Takedowns Matter More Than Damages To Performers

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://deadline.com/2026/11/sag-aftra-ai-likeness-misuse-takedown-damages-1237222661/

In an era of deepfakes, performers whose likenesses are misused by AI mostly want that content taken down rather than to go after damages, according to Duncan Crabtree-Ireland, CEO of SAG-AFTRA.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i would say the vast majority, 90-plus percent of the time, that’s what it’s about,” crabtree-ireland said at web summit in lisbon. “It’s not someone wants to get into litigation and make money. They want it to stop because they don’t agree with it, they don’t want their image used that way. It’s wrong. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the sag-aftra topper was speaking at a deadline-moderated session at web summit entitled ‘hollywood’s identity crisis’. He recalled his own experience of having his likeness misused while his members were on strike in 2023, before foregrounding the proposed No Fakes Act, which would give people greater control over their own voice and likeness. Related Stories News Web Summit Cancels Day Two As Storm Charles Hits Lisbon News Hollywood Unions Wonder Whether Next California Governor Will Share Newsom's Commitment To Expanding Film Tax Credits.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “people deserve the right to have a say in what words come out of their mouth and what they appear to be doing online. What it’s really about is getting platforms to take stuff down when your image, likeness and voice is being used without your permission. And to quell any fears, it’s really not about suing people and making a lot of money. A system like the No Fakes Act would provide that. ” Watch on Deadline.

Berdasarkan laporan, ai was the main talking point at web summit, and crabtree-ireland was asked if he detected a shift in his members’ attitudes toward the technology. “I think that there’s been a sense that if we put the right basic rules in place, that there is a way to coexist with AI,” he said. ”There’s been an understanding and an acceptance of the fact that no one can stop it, no one can block it. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa he added that a portion of sag aftra membership remains staunch ai refuseniks. But the reality is, if I were estimating, I’d say that’s something like 10%, maybe 15% [of members]. I know, I hear from them every day and they’re angry that we aren’t. “Some of our members would like us to block it. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there is also the portion of sag-aftra that wants to use ai to augment their work. “Some of our members really want to work with AI tools for augmentation, but none of them want to be replaced by AI because they love the act of creation, that’s why they do this. What you want to do is have the chance to do it, and yes, have tools that help you expand your creativity. That’s the sweet spot.

Diungkapkan bahwa “frankly, we could settle on that and then send the rest of the ai resources toward curing more diseases or some other things like that. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, crabtree-ireland was speaking on web summit’s enormous main stage, where, earlier in the week, ai-generated performer tilly norwood had been a guest. The SAG-AFTRA boss was at pains to highlight the difference between fully synthetic characters and AI replicas of real performers.

Berdasarkan laporan, “it’s important that we distinguish between humans and algorithmic outputs because an ai character, an ai asset, a generative ai-created character is not a person. One of the bigger problems we have with AI in general is we are anthropomorphizing AI models and robots and blurring the lines between humanity and non-human, artificially created entities. It doesn’t have the life of a person; it doesn’t have the experience of a person. ”.

#26. Snoopy & Woodstock's 10 Greatest Comics In Peanuts History

📅 13 Nov 2026

Snoopy & Woodstock's 10 Greatest Comics In Peanuts History

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/snoopy-woodstock-greatest-comics-peanuts/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, few friendships in comic strip history are as entertaining or heartwarming as the one shared by snoopy and woodstock in peanuts. For nearly 50 years, Charles M. Schulz brought these two beloved characters together for countless hilarious adventures and surprisingly profound moments. From their endearing friendship to their unforgettable comedic antics, Snoopy and Woodstock have created some of the Peanuts' best moments.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, whether they're embarking on another chaotic beagle scouts expedition or enjoying one of their iconic, yet unintelligible, conversations atop snoopy's red doghouse, these two always find a way to make even the simplest moments memorable. With so many comics celebrating their friendship, we're looking back at 10 of Snoopy and Woodstock's greatest strips in Peanuts history.

Sebagaimana diketahui, snoopy sitting atop his doghouse and typing away on his typewriter as he pursues his dream of becoming a famous novelist is one of the beagle’s most iconic recurring gags, resulting in some of the pup’s most hilarious strips. However, the hilarity is cranked up a notch when Schulz adds Woodstock to the mix.

Berdasarkan laporan, in this strip, we see snoopy typing away when woodstock takes it upon himself to become snoopy’s editor, suggesting through his nonsensical chirping that snoopy change his previous prose of “always remember that beauty is only fur deep” to “feather deep. ” Not many people would appreciate unsolicited writing advice, but Snoopy takes it in stride.

Sebagaimana diketahui, like snoopy, woodstock has his own fair share of recurring gags, and among the most beloved is the little bird's love for snowflakes. This recurring gag also often features Snoopy sitting atop his doghouse, silently judging Woodstock's fascination.

The strip above is one of the best examples of this recurring gag, as it shows Woodstock falling in love with two snowflakes, only for Snoopy to give up watching his friend and lie down on his doghouse, wondering, “Can a person really be in love with two different snowflakes at the same time?”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, some of snoopy and woodstock’s best moments unsurprisingly take place atop the roof of snoopy’s doghouse. The comic above, though, is a double whammy, as it also showcases Snoopy and Woodstock sharing food, another recurring activity between the two friends.

Berdasarkan laporan, here, snoopy learns that, unlike himself, woodstock prefers his ice cream cone with chocolate on the bottom and vanilla on top, the opposite of snoopy’s own preference. We wholeheartedly agree with Woodstock that this is the correct way to layer ice cream; what about you?.

While the two best friends share plenty of peaceful, heartwarming moments, they have also contributed to some of Peanuts' most hilarious comic strips, with many of these funny moments stemming from absurd misunderstandings.

Berdasarkan laporan, the strip above shows snoopy discovering that he mistook february 2's groundhog day for "ground hugs day. " A few panels later, we see Woodstock hugging the ground, making it clear that Snoopy has passed along his hilarious misunderstanding to Woodstock, resulting in the little bird spending the day hugging the ground.

Berdasarkan laporan, the strip above shows snoopy napping atop his doghouse when an exhausted woodstock lands on his mouth and nose. With his breathing now obstructed, Snoopy startles awake as he gasps for air, only for Woodstock to make himself comfortable and fall asleep on Snoopy’s nose. The beagle then thinks, “Must have been a rough flight. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the fact that snoopy makes no attempt to remove the little bird from his face is beyond heartwarming and shows just how sweet their relationship is and how deep their bond runs. Woodstock using Snoopy as his personal perch has become one of the strip’s most iconic visuals, and it remains beloved to this day.

Diungkapkan bahwa beagle scout leader snoopy is perhaps one of the pup’s most legacy-defining recurring gags, featuring snoopy leading woodstock and his fellow bird scouts on camping trips and outdoor adventures. This recurring gag went on to inspire Peanuts book collections and graphic novels, theme park attractions, and even an Apple TV+ animated series titled Camp Snoopy.

Diungkapkan bahwa that's an incredible legacy for a recurring gag, and this list of the greatest snoopy and woodstock comics would be incomplete without mentioning it. The strip above is one of our personal favorite Beagle Scout comics.

Diungkapkan bahwa the love snoopy has for woodstock is perhaps the greatest thing about the duo, and one of the best examples of snoopy’s ride-or-die energy for his little friend can be found in the strip above. Here, we see Snoopy explaining Thanksgiving to Woodstock, including the tradition of roasting a turkey. However, Woodstock gets scared at the mention of roasting, fearing that he might end up on the menu himself.

Diungkapkan bahwa snoopy then reassures his friend with a hug, promising that no one will roast him and that if anyone dares to try, he'll punch them in the nose. Snoopy, of course, acts out his promise, inadvertently punching poor, unlucky Charlie Brown in the nose and adding some hilarity to an otherwise heartwarming moment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, every snoopy fan is more than familiar with his flying ace persona, one of the beagle’s most iconic recurring alter egos in peanuts, in which he imagines himself as a daring world war i fighter pilot battling his nemesis, the infamous red baron. However, this isn't Snoopy's only sky-riding persona.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, snoopy has also imagined himself as a helicopter, with woodstock serving as his pilot. The strip above, though, shows Snoopy experiencing some dreaded engine failure. Rather than going down with Snoopy, Woodstock parachutes to safety, leaving the beagle to crash alone and make a hilarious comment about his pilot's lack of loyalty.

Sebagaimana diketahui, peanuts fans know that while we get to hear snoopy's dialogue through his thought bubbles, any "dialogue" from woodstock remains unintelligible, at least to us human readers. Snoopy, on the other hand, understands Woodstock perfectly, leading to some amusing one-sided conversations from the readers' perspective.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the strip above, we see snoopy becoming emotional over what woodstock is telling him, with the beagle commenting, “it's the way he tells it…” as though woodstock has a profound way with words. The humor comes from the fact that, to the reader, Woodstock's heartfelt speech is nothing more than complete gibberish.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while snoopy and woodstock’s interactions are typically defined by hilarity and heartwarming moments, the two also have their fair share of opportunities to impart profound wisdom to readers in an entertaining way. In the strip above, we see Snoopy and Woodstock sitting together, with Snoopy answering the little bird’s off-panel question by saying, “No, our kind doesn't get to vote. We don't have anything to say about what goes on in the world. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa woodstock then gets up and returns to his egg, humorously implying that he'd rather return to his unborn state than live in a world where he has no say in anything. While the moment is hilarious, it also offers a profound reminder to human readers: we decide what happens in this world, and the consequences of those decisions affect not only us but all other living creatures on the planet. With that great power comes the responsibility to do right by these other creatures.

This strip conveys one of Peanuts' most profound and meaningful messages, delivered through Snoopy and Woodstock.

Calvin and Hobbes is full of profound life lessons, proving that even a mischievous six-year-old can offer one of comics’ greatest insights on love.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the result is red ink, which had its world premiere at the toruńcamerimage festival this week. Co-directed by Murray and Christensen, from a script by Christensen and Murray serving as cinematographer, the film is a low-budget, noir-inspired newsroom thriller. With vampires.

Diungkapkan bahwa set over a single morning in november 1949, red ink unfolds inside the bustling headquarters of verity press, a new york times-style newspaper. Berdasarkan laporan, for the technical execution, murray turned to the same camera system used on adolescence: the dji ronin 4d, which enables extended continuous camera movements across four axes, adding a vertical dimension to the traditional three-axis pan, tilt and roll of a gimbal. Although Red Ink plays as a single take, Murray assembled the final version from “around 13 shots of 8-10 minutes each. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa red ink wasn’t supposed to be incline studios’ first feature, but it serves as an appropriate calling card for the kind of movies the company wants to make: scrappy independent features that sit between ip-driven blockbusters and the darker, less accessible dramas that dominate the arthouse space. A post-credit sequence even sets up the world of Blood Bank, bringing the filmmakers back to the project that started it all.

Next on Incline’s slate is Engaged, an adventure comedy set in Malta that Murray compares in tone to Indiana Jones.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we think there’s a gap in the independent space for movies of the kind we love,” says murray, “fun, more mainstream films with original stories. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we want to break the mold, to bring validation back to the indie space,” adds christensen. “I think with all the doom and gloom in the world, people are ready to feel hopeful again, at least at the movies. ”.

#32. IDFA Artistic Director Isabel Arrate Fernandez On Festival’s Competition Lineups, “Huge” Interest In Elizabeth Holmes Doc, And AI In Documentaries

IDFA Artistic Director Isabel Arrate Fernandez On Festival’s Competition Lineups, “Huge” Interest In Elizabeth Holmes Doc, And AI In Documentaries

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://deadline.com/2026/11/idfa-2026-isabel-arrate-fernandez-interview-1237222639/

The 39th edition of IDFA – the world’s biggest nonfiction film festival – is underway in Amsterdam, gathering the documentary field’s top talents, Oscar seekers and emerging filmmakers with dynamic work.

Berdasarkan laporan, “it’s hectic, all the last-minute things,” artistic director isabel arrate fernandez told deadline just before the kickoff. “From the lineup competitions to also the industry program we have, there are many exciting things going on. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the opening night slot friday evening goes to white tiger column, a world premiere directed by robert mentov, dwight jantzi, and bryan dickie that’s set within the resistance movement opposing myanmar’s military-dominated regime. The festival calls it “a striking example of documentary cinema… The film offers a moving portrait of a courageous generation. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, white tiger column is programmed in international competition, along with films from morocco, madagascar, burkina faso, brazil, france, germany, the republic of georgia, and other countries. An Incomplete Day in the History of Georgia 10. Considering Vladimir Putin’s attempt to reassert Russian dominance over much of the old USSR – including Ukraine – it’s a film with immediate relevance. 06. 93, directed by Salomé Jashi, examines a critical moment for Georgia in 1993 when the country, recently freed from Soviet domination, debated measures to replace the Russian ruble. Watch on Deadline.

Diungkapkan bahwa a baker’s dozen of features is programmed in the festival’s envision section, which platforms films with bold stylistic choices. “The way we look at both of our competitions,” Arrate Fernandez notes, “they are of equal value… In Envision, we are really looking at filmmakers that are challenging documentary, are challenging the form. ” Arrate Fernandez adds, “If we don’t have that, then how does a genre, how does cinema evolve?”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one of the envision titles, ragazzi al fiume, examines the experience of three young afghan immigrants to switzerland. The IDFA program notes the documentary directed by Pablo Briones “gradually evolves into an observational portrait of isolation, loss, and the longing for a peaceful future. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa fellow envision competition documentary the black box is orange focuses on the israeli town of shlomi that “was built on land belonging to the destroyed palestinian village of al-bassa, near the lebanese border,” according to the idfa program. “Beginning with the Nakba mass displacement of Palestinians in 1948, its residents were forced out and citizens of the newly established state of Israel were settled there. All traces of the previous inhabitants were to be destroyed, including all Palestinian archives. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that film is directed by yuula benivolski, an israeli jewish filmmaker born in canada and raised in the village of shlomi. (Two years ago, she posted a video on YouTube discussing her decision to renounce her Israeli citizenship. “It wasn’t a decision I made lightly… Yes, I did it in response to Israel’s horrific assault on Gaza,” she explained, before adding, “Whether Israel realizes it or not, all this death harms its own people as well. ”).

Diungkapkan bahwa more than 250 films are programmed across the festival’s sections. Among them are some of the strongest contenders for Oscars, including To Hold a Mountain, the Sundance winner directed by Biljana Tutorov and Petar Glomazić; Once Upon a Time in Harlem, directed by David Greaves and based upon material shot by his father, William Greaves (this festival is separately screening a large selection of William Greaves’s work); Musk, directed by Alex Gibney; Closure, directed by Michał Marczak, and You Can See Everything, the box office sensation about Elizabeth Holmes that’s directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim. Do they know the imprisoned Theranos founder in the Netherlands? Maybe so, maybe not, but enthusiasm for the film has certainly crossed the Atlantic.

Berdasarkan laporan, interest in you can see everything “has been huge,” arrate fernandez affirms. “The festival screenings sold out very quickly… It’s definitely generated some attention, to put it mildly. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, idfa has become an increasingly important stop for filmmakers in oscar contention, in part because of the plethora of academy documentary branch voters who are expected to attend. “Let’s see. (“It’s difficult to count them, I can tell you,” Arrate Fernandez notes. ”). Last year’s winner in IDFA’s International Competition, A Fox Under a Pink Moon, has become a leading contender for Oscar consideration this year. (That film’s protagonist and co-director, the young artist Soraya Akhlaghi, designed this year’s IDFA’s poster and contributed artwork used in the festival trailer. Watch it below).

Arrate Fernandez mentions other films in the 2026 IDFA lineup making a strong bid for Oscar recognition.

Diungkapkan bahwa “the winner of cannes, rehearsals for a revolution; traces, a ukrainian film talking about sexual assault as a war crime against women; closure, naza… there are many interesting films there that i hope will make it,” she says. “Even though they are not the films with the bigger budgets and everything for their campaigning, I really hope they get far. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, 14th, another top oscar contender that will screen at idfa, is among the documentaries that make use of ai – in the case of ava duvernay’s film, to animate vintage photographs. For the first time ever, the artistic director tells us, IDFA asked filmmakers to complete a form indicating if they had incorporated AI into their film’s production.

Diungkapkan bahwa “last year, we noticed that sometimes we were wondering while watching films and now we have this, we can go back and see what they filled out just to understand,” arrate fernandez comments. “But also, it’s part of the conversations that are taking place with regards to how to use [AI], what is acceptable? There are so many questions, so I think that really [speaks] to conversations that are being held within the industry. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, to that end, idfa will be hosting two panel discussions on ai, part of a robust lineup of industry talks. Fellow panelists include Sofía Bordenave, director of Forest Up in the Mountain, and Mohanad Yaqubi, director of Revolutionaries Never Die. A panel titled “Fighting Back – Cinema as an act of resistance?” will feature Oscar winner Laura Poitras, who is bringing They’re Here to IDFA, a short film she directed with Rachel Lauren Mueller that examines the fatal ICE surge in Minneapolis. Fernandez is slated to moderate a conversation with this year’s IDFA Guest of Honor, filmmaker Tatiana Huezo.

Berdasarkan laporan, this is the second year of arrate fernandez’s leadership as artistic director. Last year, she faced questions after IDFA revealed it would not invite to the festival what it considered to be Israeli state-supported organizations, such as DocAviv. On its website, IDFA spells out its position under a section titled “Principles and guidelines” governing the 2026 festival.

Diungkapkan bahwa “for films, makers, and organizations from countries where freedom of expression is under pressure or human rights are violated, it is essential to assess and investigate their independence carefully, alongside the artistic selection process,” idfa writes. “In this way, we aim to prevent governments and organizations involved in and/or suspected of serious human rights violations from gaining a platform at IDFA. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the idfa policy statement continues, “films, makers, and organizations are never excluded on the basis of their origin and/or nationality, but rather on the basis of any possible relationship with regimes or organizations held internationally accountable for serious human rights violations. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa arrate fernandez tells deadline, “we also really looked at what we did last year, how we’re implementing things, what are our internal processes. At the same time, it’s not a blanket approach in the sense of, ‘Oh, this financier, it’s out. And basically, for… a film work or a film project, everything just went through the regular route of being evaluated by our different teams of programmers on the creative criteria. And the moment that films make it through the different phases and end up on a short list, then in cases of countries… that are known for human rights violations, we check the independence of this film or of this project in the sense of also going about checking credits, who are financiers. ’ We also look at the film, so we still have our case-by-case approach. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, she continued, “then in terms of accreditations… we have the similar line in the sense of having this case-by-case approach. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, american israeli filmmaker rachel leah jones (advocate) will be presenting her new project, podium (you have three minutes), at idfa forum, the event’s pitching, co-financing and co-production market for nonfiction and new media projects. Logline: “What does resistance sound like when delivered from the parliamentary podium? Since Israel’s founding, Palestinian lawmakers have taken the mic to appeal, demand, denounce, and warn — articulating a powerful counter-history of the state itself. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa avi mograbi, described in the idfa program as “one of israel’s most distinguished filmmakers,” heads to the festival for the dutch premiere of his short documentary wild asparagus (halayon), which bowed at the venice film festival. In Collapse, Israeli director Anat Even returns to Kibbutz Nir Oz, where she lost her home and friends in the Hamas sneak attack of October 7, 2023. ” (The program description includes this note: “This film contains content on potentially sensitive topics. “An introspective and revealing film essay on loss, grief, revenge, dehumanization and indifference. #33. Jensen Huang’s Biopic Feels Inevitable — The Right One Might Be Impossible

Jensen Huang’s Biopic Feels Inevitable — The Right One Might Be Impossible

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/jensen-huang-biopic-inevitable-1235227381/

Diungkapkan bahwa hollywood loves a visionary, especially one whose biggest gamble eventually made him a billionaire. But the trouble with making a biopic about a tech mogul actively shaping the future? That kind of story often refuses to sit still long enough to be told before ending in calamity.

Berdasarkan laporan, when it comes to nvidia co-founder jensen huang, any filmmaker hoping to get ahead of the microchip company’s uncertain next chapter may already be too late. Or is it still… too early?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on thursday, nvidia announced that huang had resigned as ceo and board member, effective immediately. And no reason was given for the departure: a rather extraordinary development for someone who helped build the company into one of the most powerful and lucrative forces in artificial intelligence. For Hollywood, it’s the kind of twist that practically demands a screenplay. Related Stories Miles Teller Opens Up About ‘Paper Tiger,’ Adam Driver, and Losing His Home Before Filming James Gray’s Movie Fall Festival Movies Sold: ‘Woman Unknown,’ May el-Toukhy’s Golden Lion Winner, Sells to Cohen Media Group.

Diungkapkan bahwa huang’s rise from teenage denny’s employee to the face of the ai boom always had the makings of a prestige drama. Now there’s a corporate disaster — involving an alleged Chinese espionage operation and reports of multiple extramarital affairs — at the end of it. Hot dog! Still, it’s anyone’s guess whether that fiery conclusion can seem genuinely relevant by the time film and TV creatives get around to adapting it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the entertainment industry has spent much of 2026 demonstrating how difficult it is to dramatize silicon valley while the real people involved keep making headlines. 5 million in North America. Aaron Sorkin’s “The Social Reckoning,” for example, opened to just $5. That’s a disappointing debut for the follow-up to David Fincher’s “The Social Network,” which won three Oscars including best adapted screenplay.

Revisiting Facebook through the perspectives of whistleblower Frances Haugen (Mikey Madison) and Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz (Jeremy Allen White), Sorkin attempted to turn Mark Zuckerberg (Jeremy Strong) and his social media platform’s disastrous effects on politics and public discourse into a satisfying sequel.

Diungkapkan bahwa of course, audiences had already spent years living with the very real consequences of zuckerberg’s company’s actions. And in his “D+” review for IndieWire, Ryan Lattanzio described Sorkin’s approach as “less old-fashioned than completely out of date,” criticizing a falsely triumphant finale that failed to reconcile how little had actually changed in the world after the investigation’s revelations came to light.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while sorkin was late to the party, luca guadagnino’s “artificial” has had the good fortune of arriving right as things have been starting to get worse. Dramatizing OpenAI’s chaotic 2023 firing and rehiring of Sam Altman (Andrew Garfield), the dark comedy finds absurdity in the gap between Big Tech’s grandiose promises and the frequently clownish folks making them.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in his “b-” review for indiewire, david ehrlich praised the coming film for recognizing how “deeply fucking stupid the road to superintelligence has turned out to be. (Suffice to say, any film that tries to predict the cultural conversation also risks declaring history finished too soon. ” He also questioned its tendency to simplify an ongoing story into something more resolved than it is. ).

Diungkapkan bahwa “artificial” has benefited from some remarkable timing, too. Amazon MGM dropped the project after entering into a partnership with OpenAI — with sources telling the Los Angeles Times that the script’s critical perspective on artificial intelligence specifically contributed to the decision. Neon eventually acquired it, and a well-received New York Film Festival premiere helped build some serious awards-season momentum for routine Oscar contender Guadagnino.

Sebagaimana diketahui, then came the u. S. midterms, during which voters across the country backed restrictions on data-center development. That makes the questions about who controls AI and who actually pays for its consequences feel spectacularly urgent, effectively turning a simple boardroom fight into a existential consideration of society with significantly heavier stakes.

Of course, tech biopics don’t necessarily have to predict the future to be powerful.

Berdasarkan laporan, consider hulu’s “the dropout,” which won amanda seyfried an emmy for playing theranos founder elizabeth holmes. Four years later, Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s boundary-breaking documentary “You Can See Everything” once again made Holmes a viral sensation — even bringing Seyfried into contact with the woman she portrayed.

Diungkapkan bahwa as indiewire tv critic ben travers recently argued, “the dropout” remains effective precisely because it didn’t pretend to know everything about holmes in 2022. Fielder and Oppenheim’s contribution often gets so close to its subject that Holmes’ motives become difficult to pin down, while the series maintains enough separation to keep her actions and victims in focus.

“Sometimes a healthy distance provides greater clarity,” Travers wrote.

Berdasarkan laporan, that’s a useful lesson for anyone hoping to next adapt the life of a silicon valley billionaire before history has finished passing judgment on them. And in Huang’s case, there’s already plenty of material to work with — before pretending to know how his former employer’s whole saga ends.

Diungkapkan bahwa having cofounded nvidia in 1993, huang nearly lost the company after betting on a method of rendering video-game graphics that microsoft effectively rendered obsolete. With Nvidia running out of money, he then scrapped its original technology and made a last-ditch gamble on a new chip that ultimately helped save the business.

Diungkapkan bahwa huang eventually helped develop the graphics-processing infrastructure that would make his company’s hardware essential to the ai boom. Fast-forward to a public apology to his wife and throw in a leather jacket? Hollywood could probably have a trailer ready by Christmas.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but that would also be the easiest, and potentially least interesting, version of huang’s story, right? nvidia’s success was built on the backs of countless engineers, researchers, and developers aside from huang. The fallout within the AI giant will impact everyone.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a truly great movie about huang and nvidia would need to understand the company’s founding and survival, follow the enormous risks huang took with that future, and then seriously interrogate what happens when a single corporation becomes indispensable to the technology rapidly reshaping nearly all of modern life. Those are three(!) very different artistic ambitions. Considering the entertainment industry’s own increasingly lucrative partnerships with AI companies, and Amazon’s offloading of “Artificial,” there’s reason to wonder just how much scrutiny Hollywood would be willing to apply to the innovators they are in business with.

Which brings us back to the question of when to make a Jensen Huang biopic.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the tech industry is moving faster than filmmakers can reasonably hope to keep up with, but the bigger problem may be that news around the silicon valley story most worth telling is changing just as quickly. A film about the man who helped build the future we’re facing might have been an easy sell a few years ago. These days, the more pressing issue is what kind of world Huang actually put in motion — and whether Hollywood can afford to doubt it in public.

Diungkapkan bahwa misty interrupts her life of boozing and bar pickups when her brother donny (paul sparks) calls asking for her help following the disappearance of his 22-year-old daughter charlie hart (rising country star carter faith in a passable acting debut). Even though she has gone AWOL and resurfaced in the past — showing up late or not at all for concerts and disappointing her fans — Donny is convinced she’s in trouble after being unable to reach her for three days. Charlie has become a significant music figure in a relatively short time, pumping out 10 albums and touring nonstop. With his wife undergoing cancer treatment, Donny can’t go to Nashville to look for Charlie, so he convinces her abrasive estranged aunt to go instead.

Sebagaimana diketahui, even before misty arrives back in music city, donny steers her toward two suspects — jared granger (jp edwards), a sicko stalker whose attentions prompted charlie to take out a restraining order; and her boyfriend jace jacobs (ross lynch), a cocky young country rocker whose romantic duets with charlie tell a different story to their real relationship. Neither Donny nor Misty buys the statement of Charlie’s manager Kelly (Wynn Everett) that she’s merely taking a break on a songwriting retreat.

Sebagaimana diketahui, frustrated that the cops have turned up nothing, misty tries putting pressure on them. But her sharp elbows get her stonewalled by Detective White (Norbert Leo Butz), who recalls she was once known as “The Queen of Mean. ” “No, it was actually the C**t of Country,” replies Misty, reworking a line that once got Carlene Carter into trouble. Charlie’s history of sudden disappearances means the cops don’t take the case seriously.

Diungkapkan bahwa reconnecting with her old musician friend bucky (ben dickey) at a bar, misty meets record label owner roy combs (garrett hedlund), who has a reputation for launching new talents at the venue and was the architect of charlie’s ascendancy. Despite their mutual attraction, Misty keeps Roy at arm’s length in subsequent encounters.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, no sooner has bucky warned her to tread carefully — nashville has changed and she no longer has the protection of being famous — than misty gets run off the road by a pickup truck while driving at night. She also comes home to find evidence of an intruder. Only when she goes looking for clues at Charlie’s house, finding blood and signs of a disturbance, then stumbles onto her niece’s bloodied sweats in Granger’s shed does Det. White announce to press that the missing person case has now become an active murder investigation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, by this point, the audience should be pulled into the mystery, especially as secrets come tumbling out, starting with a bombshell misty drops on a tv talkshow. But Feste’s script lacks the tension or dread to build dramatic momentum, even as new elements come to light and Misty finds herself in serious danger. One problem is that two of the main suspects are too painfully obvious to be guilty, while the real culprit is easy to guess, well before Charlie turns up to provide answers.

Berdasarkan laporan, chastain was coached in vocals, piano and guitar for the role, doing all her own singing with assurance. There’s some appeal in watching Misty take over when antagonistic Jace pulls her out on stage during one of his shows or hearing her belt out the title song alongside country royalty Winnie Jo Lean (Jennifer Nettles, bringing strong pipes and folksy sparkle to a two-scene role).

Berdasarkan laporan, but chastain was better served by the twangy vocal opportunities of george & tammy or the gospel fervor of the eyes of tammy faye, which bagged her a best actress oscar for one of her least memorable films. Though she does get to say lines like “I’ma go get my gun. There’s a rich history of Hollywood actresses persuasively inhabiting country music stars — Reese Witherspoon in Walk the Line, Sissy Spacek and Beverly D’Angelo in Coal Miner’s Daughter, Karen Black in Altman’s Nashville — but Heartland doesn’t give Chastain anything close to that kind of space to shine. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, naturally, pretty-voiced faith also performs her own songs here, as do lynch as jace and john hawkes in a brief appearance as misty’s ex-husband. The weak link in the cast is Hedlund (reuniting with Feste after Country Strong), who communicates little of Roy’s shifty charisma, beyond the sign stapled to his forehead with the word “corrupt” in bold red letters. More than any actor’s shortcomings, however, the big issue is the director’s tendency to let the film keep going slack when it should be tightening the knot. Unable to foster much emotional investment in its characters, it’s Country Weak.

#49. The 10 Most Masterful Climaxes in Animated Movies

📅 13 Nov 2026

The 10 Most Masterful Climaxes in Animated Movies

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://collider.com/animated-movies-most-masterful-endings/

There are spoilers ahead for the climax of each entry!.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, several of the greatest animated films of all time have likewise delivered some of the most exciting, dramatic, and memorable climaxes in film history. Animation is, after all, a practically limitless medium, capable of visually achieving practically anything a filmmaker can set their mind to. Indeed, many artists throughout history have taken full advantage of animation's boundless potential.

Berdasarkan laporan, whether it's a deeply emotional third act like the one in the iron giant or a grand, exciting final battle like that of wildwood, the best animated movie climaxes in history are proof that artists really can achieve pretty much anything through this unique medium. Not coincidentally, these happen to be among the most riveting and widely beloved animated movies in the history of the Seventh Art.

Berdasarkan laporan, after writing matthew robbins' 1987 sci-fi dramedy batteries not included, brad bird made his directorial debut with the iron giant, now remembered as one of the most perfect animated movies of all time. Based on the novel The Iron Giant by Ted Hughes, it's about a boy who befriends a large alien robot and tries to protect him from a paranoid American government agent during the Cold War.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the whole film is substantially different from the source material, which only ends up working in its favor throughout—including during the deeply emotional and irresistibly exciting climax. However, a nuclear missile is sent their way, so the Giant decides to sacrifice himself to save the town. After the Giant's built-in lethal defense protocol takes over, Hogarth manages to calm him down. It's impossible to not grow profoundly fond of these characters as the story goes on; and as such, it's impossible not to be moved to tears by this whole third act.

Berdasarkan laporan, people who look down on animation as a medium inferior to live-action have clearly never experienced the works of satoshi kon, whose perfect blue is one of the best animated thriller movies in history. Loosely based on Yoshikazu Takeuchi's novel Perfect Blue: Complete Metamorphosis, the film follows a former pop idol who transitions to a serious acting career, but begins to lose her grip on reality as an obsessed stalker starts to close in on her.

Sebagaimana diketahui, after it's revealed that the mastermind behind mima's suffering was always her manager, rumi, a psychotic rumi begins to chase mima with the intention of murdering her. It's an incredibly intense and adrenaline-pumping climax, with some of the most stunning visuals and most frenetic editing of any anime movie in history. Mima managing to assert control of her identity, choosing to save Rumi's life, is a deeply satisfying moment that finally grants audiences a chance to breathe.

Sebagaimana diketahui, just because the whole shrek franchise has become the subject of endless memes as the years have passed, people shouldn't allow themselves to forget that this is one of the most groundbreaking animated movie series in history. As for Shrek 2, where Shrek and Fiona travel to see the princess' skeptical parents after returning from their honeymoon, it's genuinely one of the greatest animated comedies in film history.

Diungkapkan bahwa sure, it's one of the funniest fantasy movies of all time, but it also knows exactly when to get seriously emotional—and exactly when to get grand and exciting. The film's climax sees Shrek and the gang storming the castle of Far Far Away to save Fiona from the Fairy Godmother and Prince Charming's lies, all to the beat of a legendary rendition of Bonnie Tyler's "Holding Out for a Hero. " It's a climax as exciting as it is funny, charming, and genuinely emotional.

Diungkapkan bahwa based on his own 1982 manga, katsuhiro otomo's akira is one of the most important and highly influential anime films in history, having greatly helped popularize japanese animation in the western world. It's a cyberpunk masterpiece set in a futuristic dystopian Neo-Tokyo, where a teenage biker gang leader must race to save his best friend from a secretive military experiment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, all in all, akira is one of the most perfect animated movies of the 1980s, and that includes a climax that's beyond iconic and beyond viscerally tense. Consumed by his pain and ego, Tetsuo mutates into an all-engulfing monster, engulfing Neo-Tokyo in a blinding light and birthing a new universe. Visually stunning and tragic to the core, it's a thematically and emotionally dense climax that's impossible to look away from.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the 21st century, dreamworks animation properly established itself as one of hollywood's animation studio titans, but they were already making masterpieces as far back as 1998. The Prince of Egypt is one of the best animated movies in film history, an epic musical about the adopted Egyptian prince Moses discovering his hidden Hebrew heritage, and being chosen by God to liberate his enslaved people from his Pharaoh brother.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it's one of the most enrapturing biblical stories ever conveyed on the big screen, and proof that faith-based cinema can be absolutely masterful and universally endearing. Its climax is the same as that of the Book of Exodus, with Moses parting the Red Sea and rushing his people through with the Egyptians hot on their heels. On top of having some of the most gorgeous visuals of any climax from any 20th-century animated film, this whole sequence is also one that's surprisingly tragic and poignant for a family film.

Berdasarkan laporan, after the success of the shrek franchise, a spin-off didn't take long to materialize. 2011's Puss in Boots, however, is often remembered as one of DreamWorks' middle-of-the-road efforts. Puss in Boots: The Last Wish, on the other hand, is one of their best efforts to date, following Puss' journey to find the mythical Wishing Star in order to restore his eight lost lives while being hunted by Death itself.

Berdasarkan laporan, there's a wide variety of reasons why the last wish is one of the best animated films of the 2020s so far, not least of which is its electrifying climax. A fight between the film's various main characters, a final duel between Death and Puss, and some of the most stunning and vibrant visuals of any animated feature in history. What more could any fan of the medium possibly ask for?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, back in 1995, pixar revolutionized the film industry as a whole with the release of toy story, the first feature film ever created entirely through cgi. But as incredible as it and Toy Story 2 are, it's Toy Story 3 that's regarded by many as Pixar's best film to date. In it, Andy's toys are accidentally donated to a daycare center before he leaves for college, forcing the gang to execute a daring escape to return to their owner.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, before one of the most perfect movie endings of the 2010s comes one of the most perfect movie climaxes in animation history: after escaping from the daycare, the toys are trapped and taken to the city landfill. They're almost incinerated after Lotso betrays them, only to be rescued at the eleventh hour by the Little Green Men. It's arguably the darkest, scariest, and saddest climax of any Pixar film, followed by an absolutely triumphant (and perfectly excusable) deus ex machina and a denouement that's just as spotless.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it took laika, the undisputed masters of modern-day stop-motion animation, a whopping 16 years in total to adapt colin melloy's fantasy novel wildwood for the big screen. Boy, was the wait worth it. The film follows Prue, who ventures into a magical forest after her baby brother is abducted, finding herself caught up in the midst of a brewing civil war.

Diungkapkan bahwa recency bias be damned: wildwood can already very reasonably be called one of the best animated fantasy movies in history. Much like the greatest epic fantasy films, it ends with a momentous final battle and the emotional and thematic culmination of both the protagonist's and the villain's journeys. With some incredible music, excellent writing, and animation that's genuinely jaw-dropping from the beginning to the end of the sequence, it single-handedly makes the price of admission worth every penny.

Diungkapkan bahwa regarded by many animation fans as pixar's best outing to date, ratatouille is one of those animated films that are perfect from start to finish. It follows Remy, a rat who dreams of becoming a gourmet chef. After finding a clumsy kitchen worker named Linguini, the two form an alliance so that Remy can secretly cook at a famous Parisian restaurant, controlling Linguini's arms by pulling on his hair. It sounds like a silly premise on paper, but Brad Bird is able to do some absolute wonders with it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, where many family films' climaxes come in the form of cathartic final battles or moments of adrenaline-pumping suspense, ratatouille's climax is far quieter and more subdued. With the kitchen staff having walked out in disgust after Linguini's confession that Remy has been cooking the whole time, Remy assembles his rat friends and family to help him cook a simple Ratatouille for extra-strict critic Anton Ego. Taken back to his childhood by the dish, Ego is disarmed by Remy's cooking. If any animated film climax proves that you don't need to go big in order to be memorable, it's this one.

Berdasarkan laporan, after the oscar-winning spider-man: into the spider-verse took the world by storm, expectations were through the roof for its sequel, across the spider-verse. Thankfully, it surpassed them. It continues Miles Morales' story as the Wall-Crawler, this time following him as he journeys across dimensions and rebels against a society of Spider-People to save those he loves.

Berdasarkan laporan, saying that across the spider-verse is one of the best animated movies of the last five years would be an understatement, just like it would be an understatement to say that it has an irresistibly exciting climax. Having learned from Spider-Man 2099 that his father's death is his inevitable "Canon Event," Miles refuses to accept it and manages to conduct a daring solo escape from Nueva York, facing hundreds of Spider-People on the way. It's easily the most thrilling, visually impressive, best-scored, thematically charged, and emotionally enthralling climax of any animated film in history.

#52. Avatar: The Last Airbender's New Sequel Just Changed Genres Twice In 1 Season

📅 13 Nov 2026

Avatar: The Last Airbender's New Sequel Just Changed Genres Twice In 1 Season

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/avatar-seven-havens-different-genres-last-airbender/

Berdasarkan laporan, when a tv classic starts getting spun off into sequels, it’s usually a recipe for diminishing returns. The ending of The Boys is about to be undermined by the arrival of Vought Rising, and The Walking Dead’s final episode is too busy setting up everyone’s spinoffs to provide a satisfying conclusion to the 11-season saga at hand. But franchise expansion isn’t always a bad thing. The sequels and spinoffs don’t always undermine the original; sometimes, they complement the original.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, avatar: the last airbender is one of the greatest tv shows ever made. Along with The Wire and Chernobyl and Six Feet Under, it’s one of those shows that everyone should watch at least once in their lives. It’s a martial arts fantasy epic, with lots of superpowered fight scenes, but underneath the spectacle, it deals with really dark, heavy themes, and makes big ideas accessible to small viewers.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the years since avatar went off the air, the powers that be have blown it up into a franchise, with a live-action remake, a straight-to-streaming movie sequel, and a couple of spinoff shows. While it could’ve rested on the franchise’s laurels and just copied everything that worked about The Last Airbender, Seven Havens has proven to be its own beast entirely. The latest spinoff, Avatar: Seven Havens, picks up more than 200 years after Korra’s tenure as the Avatar. It’s set in the familiar Avatar world, but it tells a brand-new story with brand-new characters and themes, and it belongs to a different genre altogether.

Berdasarkan laporan, by the time seven havens picks up, the avatar universe is a very different place than we’re used to. In The Last Airbender, everyone was being oppressed by the Fire Nation, but the world itself was intact. In Seven Havens, the world has effectively ended; all but the titular seven settlements have been wiped out by a mysterious apocalyptic event known as “The Cataclysm. ” Since the Cataclysm is believed to have been caused by Korra, the Avatar is no longer a beloved folk hero; they’re considered a harbinger of death. But it’s not just the worldbuilding that’s changed; the sequel is dabbling in a couple of new genres.

Berdasarkan laporan, the last airbender was a classical hero’s journey, following aang’s quest to get over his impostor syndrome, come to terms with his destiny, master all four elements, and defeat the fire lord. But Seven Havens brings not one, but two different genres into the fold. The futuristic sequel is both a post-apocalyptic adventure across the Mad Max-style “harshlands,” and an engaging mystery, keeping us in the dark as it slowly unravels the truth behind the Cataclysm.

Sebagaimana diketahui, rather than just rehashing what worked in the last airbender, seven havens flips the script. Suddenly, the world is over, the Avatar is a villain, and there’s a mystery to uncover. Seven Havens is the Avatar franchise’s first attempt at a Lost-style mystery-box show, and it’s been working a charm so far.

Diungkapkan bahwa seven havens is a very different story than the last airbender, set in a very different time, but it shares a tenacious spirit with its predecessor. Like The Last Airbender, Seven Havens inspires hope in the face of adversity, it deals with mature themes and trusts its young audience to wrap their little heads around them, and it allegorizes universal coming-of-age stories through the lens of mythic fantasy.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for the first time ever, there are two avatars sharing the responsibilities of the title. Pavi and Nisha are long-lost twins who discover a strange psychic connection and quickly realize that the fate of the world rests in their hands. Much like The Last Airbender did with Aang, Avatar: Seven Havens uses the high-stakes pressures of being the Avatar to reflect the relatable foibles of growing up.

Diungkapkan bahwa all of these shows share common tropes, despite disparate tones, topics, and objectives — not the least of which are their glorious feminist underpinnings. Within each of these thrillers lurk so many shady husbands, brothers, bosses, and dads. “All Her Fault” was so attuned to the ways men routinely let down their families Vulture hailed it as a “misandrist masterpiece. The patriarchy looms large enough to get name-checked, and the leading ladies are all fighting an uphill battle just to be seen, heard, and understood. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa but “long bright river” carries the most direct parallels with “the good daughter,” both by design and on accident. They’re both gritty and dark. They both follow leads whose careers connect back to their personal demons, and they both track working-class women fighting for their impoverished communities (and against the shitty men who run them). Where “All Her Fault” and “Apples Never Fall” could be carelessly devoured as melodramatic amusements, “Long Bright River” and “The Good Daughter” are too brutal and self-serious to constitute anyone’s idea of a “fun” binge, even if there is a morbid bit of fun to be found in the latter’s performances, dialogue, and many, many character quirks.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the good daughter” is set in the fictional town of pikesville, ga, where charlie (meghann fahy) works as a public defender, adjacent to her sole-surviving parent, town pariah, and private defense attorney, rusty quinn (brendan gleeson). Her mother, lovingly referred to as Gamma (Olivia Williams), didn’t live long enough to be a grandma; she was murdered in front of her daughters when they were just kids, and the resulting assaults left Charlie’s sister Sam (Rose Byrne) with a lifelong motor speech disorder called dysarthria, as well as impaired vision and a notable limp.

Berdasarkan laporan, sam is also a lawyer, but she specializes in patent law (to avoid the anxiety that comes with criminal cases) and moved to new york as soon as she was old enough to get out of georgia. She only returns to Pikeville when Rusty, for the first time, calls to say her sister needs help. Why now? Well, the list of Charlie’s hardships is nearly as long as her sister’s, but Rusty — who tends to speak in Flannery O’Connor quotes — is likely referring to the most recent trauma: a school shooting she witnessed that left the principal and a 13-year-old student dead.

Sebagaimana diketahui, once sam is back in town, the two sisters start mounting a defense for their dad’s client: the school shooter, kelly wilson (shayna benardo), an 18-year-old student with an intellectual disability. The maniacal powers that be are eager to kill her — first at the scene of a shooting, where a teacher (played by Jake McDorman) saves her from the trigger-happy cops, and then in court, where a self-righteous district attorney argues for the death penalty, competency laws be damned.

Diungkapkan bahwa they’re all under the coins’ thumb, a powerful family (with connections throughout the local government) who turned the township against rusty and his family long ago. The only folks willing to help the Quinns are Rusty’s best friend and legal aide, Lenore (Harper Steele), and Charlie’s husband and assistant district attorney, Ben (Michael Dorman). Everyone believes Charlie and Sam lied about who killed their mother, and they resent Rusty for defending so many “obviously” guilty parties. Otherwise, they’re on their own, standing up for Kelly, standing up to the Coins, and standing against Bad Men™️.

Berdasarkan laporan, adapted by karin slaughter (from her own book) and directed entirely by steph green (“duster,” “dare me”), “the good daughter” holds back too many revelations for the finale, creating an exposition-heavy ending that covers its bases but functions like an endless list of answers. It’s not as powerful as it needs to be in order to justify its upsetting subject matter, and it’s trauma-drama plotting skews into overkill well before it’s done doling out distress.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, and yet, i have to say, much of it works. The same goes for Rusty’s folksy banter, poetry quotes, and even his red-nose routine, in which the professional attorney pops on a clown nose whenever he feels the moment calls for a little levity. Such a strange, impractical choice, deployed as often as it is here, could spoil a curious character who’s always viewed from his children’s removed perspective. Maybe he’s unbelievable, maybe he’s too cute for the rest of the story, maybe he’s simply too silly. Credit goes to the cast, particularly Byrne and Gleeson, for internalizing their showy character quirks to such a degree that Sam’s limp, vision impairment, and sporadic stutter — yes, also a stutter! — never feel like her defining traits. But Gleeson gathers it all up to form a heartbroken widower who just wants to give his traumatized children the light they need in an ever-darkening world.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fresh bursts of creative southern witticisms are similarly rewarding, like hearing gleeson say, “never kick a fresh turd on a hot day” or byrne tell a patronizing windbag “to shit in both hands and start clapping. ” The series ultimately rests on Sam and Charlie’s relationship, and their relationship is strong. Their dialogue, particularly when poking fun at one another, rings true, and there’s a buddy-cop dynamic to their investigation that demands to be extended into an ongoing series.

Diungkapkan bahwa not this series, mind you. Peacock should limit this limited series to its established, er, limits. But I know a streamer where Byrne and Fahy could pitch another thriller centered around two crusading women looking to crack a case, save their souls, and destroy the patriarchy in one fell swoop.

Just maybe base the next one on a slightly easier read.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the good daughter” premieres thursday, november 12 on peacock. All six episodes will be released at once.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i think this was true indie filmmaking. Diungkapkan bahwa after i watched pop pop, i felt motivated to try harder again to keep in dialogue with people who may not always share my political or other ideas or hopes. What’s your hope for audiences of Pop Pop?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i hope it causes massive fights and wrecks entire families. No, I’m kidding! Berdasarkan laporan, so, yes, i wanted to ask how we deal with other people who we potentially don’t agree with, but we still have to be in community with.
