#104. Stacy Keach Played A Villain In One Of The Best Batman Movies Of All Time

📅 13 Nov 2026

Stacy Keach Played A Villain In One Of The Best Batman Movies Of All Time

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2315598/stacy-keach-batman-mask-of-the-phantasm-villain-role-explained/

Sebagaimana diketahui, actor stacy keach passed away on november 10, 2026, leaving behind a huge list of film, television, and theatre credits across his lifetime. Typecasting never really caught up with Keach. He could play diametrically different characters, like how he acted as both the morally upright Warden Henry Pope in "Prison Break" and Neo-Nazi leader Cameron Alexander in "American History X. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, even so, keach's deep voice often coded him as a tough guy you don't want to mess with. DC Comics and Batman fans will recognize that voice from "Batman: Mask of the Phantasm," one of the best Batman movies, animated or otherwise. The titular villain is a skull-masked, scythe-wielding vigilante targeting gangsters in Gotham City. Unlike Batman (Kevin Conroy), the Phantasm employs lethal force.

Sebagaimana diketahui, keach voices the phantasm (at least when they're wearing their mask). The Phantasm doesn't say that much, admittedly, because silence serves their menacing presence more. But whenever the Phantasm first appears in a plume of smoke, they announce themselves with this line: "[Name], your angel of death awaits!" Keach makes the Phantasm's voice live up to those words. It's deep and ghostly, with an echo that sounds like he is genuinely an apparition from beyond the mortal plane.

Diungkapkan bahwa "mask of the phantasm" features a dual timeline structure; half of the movie takes place in bruce wayne's youth before he becomes batman. Keach has a second role in this storyline as Carl Beaumont, Andrea's financier father. He romances Andrea Beaumont (Dana Delany), the woman he almost chose over becoming Batman. Naturally, you then make the leap (subconsciously or not) in thinking that Carl is the Phantasm, especially once we learn he was once indebted to the gangsters the Phantasm is killing in the present. That's just what the movie wants you to think.

Berdasarkan laporan, okay, enough hiding behind spoilers: the phantasm is actually andrea herself. But the gangsters caught up to the Beaumonts, killed Carl, and now Andrea is back for revenge. (Amusingly, the twist of Andrea being the Phantasm was spoiled by some tie-in toys. She and her father had to flee the country to dodge his loan shark debtors, which is why she canceled her engagement to Bruce all those years ago. ).

Diungkapkan bahwa keach's part as carl gets back to his acting range. Diegetically, Andrea has given her alter ego her father's voice to throw suspicion off herself. The red herring of Carl being the Phantasm becomes text late in the movie, after Andrea and Bruce rekindle their relationship and she explains why she left him — except for the part that her dad is dead. He plays, essentially, the Grim Reaper and a terrified father, and he's great in both parts. While framing her father might dishonor his memory, she's also playing the part of Carl Beaumont's vengeful spirit to kill his killers.

Diungkapkan bahwa batman having a romantic connection with a foe is nothing new — just ask catwoman or talia al ghul. "Mask of the Phantasm" commits to being a romantic tragedy; Batman doesn't reach or redeem Andrea, who chooses her vengeance. The Phantasm's backstory has the foundation for a redemption, but happy endings are hard to come by in Gotham City. The final two scenes of the film show Andrea and then Bruce, both alone again. But at least Batman still has Gotham.

Berdasarkan laporan, "mask of the phantasm" remains widely beloved and is often considered the late kevin conroy's greatest performance as batman. Stacy Keach as the Phantasm was an essential ingredient, too, and may he also rest in peace.

#109. Universal's Best Twilight / Harry Potter Replacement Has Been In Development Hell For Six Years

📅 13 Nov 2026

Universal's Best Twilight / Harry Potter Replacement Has Been In Development Hell For Six Years

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/crave-harry-potter-twilight-replacement-development-hell/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, step aside, twilight, and move over, harry potter; universal has the perfect answer to both. It may seem an unlikely combination; Twilight is a "sparkly vampire" romance, while Harry Potter blazed the trail for the current generation of magic schools (complete with a healthy dose of a Chosen One destiny). And yet, have you ever noticed how the best original stories are a delightful mix of multiple ideas, creating something refreshingly new and yet delightfully familiar?.

Berdasarkan laporan, step forward tracy wolff's crave, which is a stunning blend of the two. It stars Grace Foster, a young orphan who winds up sent to what turns out to be a school for vampires, werewolves, dragons, witches, and more. And, of course, the different groups don't get on at all. The book is delightfully self-aware (at one point the vampire love-interest gives Grace a gift copy of Twilight), and it turns so many of the central tropes upside-down in a fantastic way.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, crave launched in 2020, and it's expanded into a full six-book series. Katmere Academy isn't Hogwarts; it's much more dangerous, a little closer to the dark academia books I've fallen in love with of late. The various factions initially feel almost like your traditional high school, where the jocks and the nerds all hang out together, but it soon becomes clear the racial "tribes" are much more dangerous. Grace has no idea what she's dealing with, and initially there's an entertaining sense of denial as readers figure out what's happening even as she tries to tell herself she's going nuts.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that said, my personal favorite twist here is that the heroes are not the chosen ones. In fact, this is a franchise where the Chosen One went wrong; where the vampire love interest's brother was believed to be a Chosen One, and was raised to believe he was something special. It's fascinating to realize how much this kind of philosophy can twist and scar a person, making the Crave story a fun interrogation of a trope we've seen played out so many times. It reminds me a little of Anakin Skywalker in the Star Wars prequels, but a little better done (with apologies to George Lucas).

Berdasarkan laporan, as a lover of twilight and harry potter, and someone who very much enjoys romantasy, i can honestly say crave is a must-read. Wolff is wonderfully creative, and her world is so very immersive; even when she plays with familiar tropes and character beats, she does so with a nod and a wink. If you like vampires and werewolves, magic schools, or even dragon shifters, this is the series for you.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but here's the annoying thing; universal acquired the rights to crave before the first book even came out, with universal’s svp of production jeyun munford and creative executive christine sun set to oversee the production. We've had zero news about the film since then, though, which is something of a surprise; unfortunately, Munford isn't even at Universal anymore, which may well mean this particular movie has been lost in development hell. If so, it's a real shame; at a time when both Harry Potter and Twilight are re-emerging, this is an epic that should really be given a chance to flourish.

For now, readers would be wise to pick up Crave for something that will definitely scratch that itch in the best possible way.

He’s a cruel miser of a man who comes to learn the error of his ways over the course of a ghost story that preys upon Christian precepts of redemption and forgiveness (along with the more secular warm and fuzzies of seeing a bad guy discover the joys of being good). Indeed, what is “cancel culture” if not a shackled delusion that visits self-made pariahs in the dead of night, and what is Charles Dickens’ “A Christmas Carol” if not a plea to believe that even the most odious of souls are still capable of being saved? Related Stories Jensen Huang’s Biopic Feels Inevitable — The Right One Might Be Impossible Miles Teller Opens Up About ‘Paper Tiger,’ Adam Driver, and Losing His Home Before Filming James Gray’s Movie.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s been reported that johnny depp accepted the title role of ti west’s “ebenezer” at a fraction of his usual rate, but i suspect that he probably would have done this movie for free. While the embattled star earned more than $250 million for his work on the “Pirates of the Caribbean” franchise, even that psychotic number pales in comparison to the pricelessness of starring in a major studio Christmas movie that allows him to look just left of the camera and say lines like “I’m not the man I was!” and “I was once good, and I know I can be again!” before his character saves a cherubic little boy from certain death and invites a freezing beggar inside for a warm cup of tea. If an old crank like Scrooge can make his way back toward grace, why not the convicted star of “Mortdecai,” and the alleged perpetrator of several even more serious crimes?.

Berdasarkan laporan, johnny depp may prefer for that to be framed as a rhetorical question, but his insufferable turn as literature’s most cantankerous moneylender demands an honest answer. For me, that answer is rather straightforward: While Depp has never been the subtlest of actors, his post-Sparrow pivot away from artistic curiosity has distended his talents into such a grotesque caricature of their former charm that “Ebenezer” left me feeling like I may never be able to empathize with his screen presence again.

Sebagaimana diketahui, scrooge is obviously a scenery-chewer’s dream, but the crescent arc he traces from grinch to christmas miracle is only believable enough to sustain dickens’ fable if you believe it on both ends. Whatever my feelings about Depp as a human being, the truth is that I didn’t buy him as a glowering monster any more than I bought him as a beaming man who’s grown “better than his word. His offscreen unsavoriness certainly doesn’t help, but there’s a more immediate problem when the lights go down, one that makes him a unique case among Hollywood’s tainted array of mega-star actors: He seems to have become very bad at acting. Depp’s performance — an advent calendar of empty affectations without a soul to anchor them, every shot full of face and bereft of feeling — makes that exceedingly difficult. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa an unengaging ebenezer is a tough break for a movie called “ebenezer,” and screenwriter nathaniel halpern’s fidelity to the source material doesn’t exactly leave west with a wealth of opportunities to compensate for such fatal miscasting. As you might expect from the director of indie genre standouts like “Pearl” and “The House of the Devil,” West’s big idea is to scare the Dickens out of us by turning up the volume on this story’s implicit scariness. West’s take on the holiday classic is faithful to the core — no Muppets, no ghosts of girlfriends past, no uncanny mo-capped Jim Carrey. Sometimes literally, as this PG-13 carol offers a small handful of gentle jump-scares.

Berdasarkan laporan, “ebenezer” isn’t a horror movie in the strictest sense, but west does what he can to play up the fear that eventually terrifies scrooge into giving a shit about his fellow man. Most — or all — of those flourishes are purely cosmetic in nature, and hellbent on sucking every glimmer of life out of Victorian England. Scrooge’s office has never looked more haunted, as Checco Varese’s grimdark cinematography and Eve Stewart’s Yharnam-esque production design combine to create a London that’s in dire need of Christmas cheer (the vibe should go a long way with tweenage audiences eager for a bit of spice with their holiday viewing, though I suspect the whole thing is too staid and oppressive to become any kind of perennial favorite).

Berdasarkan laporan, and since west would sooner die than pass up a chance for death, this version of the story treats us to a musty prologue where we actually get to see ebenezer’s business partner bite the dust with his mouth wide open (marley is played by ian mckellen in what currently stands as the most “remember ‘the christophers?’” performance of the year). From there, the action skips forward to Christmas Eve 1843, whence Ebenezer is inflicting his usual “Bah, humbug!” routine on poor Bob Cratchit (Rupert Grint), the underpaid clerk he resents for taking the next day off (HR being a decidedly 20th-century invention). But the fates have plans of their own for the bitter-cold businessman, who promptly pisses himself when the ghost of old Marley bursts into his miserable bedchamber later that night.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, reaction shots ensue, as depp curdles his face into a series of the most exaggerated expressions since the death of silent cinema, every one of them betraying his character’s frigidness. This Ebenezer takes an active pleasure in being cruel, which not only makes him more detestable (which is fine), but also endows him with an innate capacity for joy that makes the rest of the movie feel like it’s walking in circles (which is less fine). Given that Depp’s performance is only as wide as his lips and as deep as his pockets, it seems wasteful that we should have to walk through the hollows of Ebenezer’s past, present, and future in order to fix him — it would be easier and equally meaningful to just push the corners of his mouth into a smile.

Berdasarkan laporan, of course, that would deprive us of the “holy shit, that’s andrea riseborough” fun of the “to leslie” star’s ghost of christmas past, a white-eyed ghoul who looks like a spirit from “the conjuring” who popped up for a sudden jolt and then forgot to leave the frame. She’s the most amusing part of a familiar tour through the sadness of Ebenezer’s childhood, where he was bullied by the other kids and kept apart from his beloved older sister. Tramell Tillman is equally compelling as the boisterous Ghost of Christmas Present, though his bizarre character design — a round-bellied man whose face appears to be rotting to pieces in real-time — turns out to be reverse-engineered from an unnerving reveal that both honors Dickens’ text and also underlines West’s limited conviction to rejuvenate it with the visceral immediacy of a horror film (his commitment to the bit falls well short of the Robert Eggers-level follow-through that conceit demands).

Diungkapkan bahwa given the emphasis the director puts on the film’s genre spin, it’s ironic and surprising that “ebenezer” is at its best when it focuses on the most basic human elements of its story, if only because the supporting characters offer such a welcome contrast to whatever depp is doing. Sam Claflin and Daisy Ridley don’t have a whole lot to do as Ebenezer’s kind-hearted nephew Fred and his wife Clara (respectively), but the film takes pains to stress how sad it is that Scrooge is Fred’s last connection to his dead mother, and it’s touching to see how much it would mean for him to have a cordial relationship with the old miser.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it is considerably less touching to see ebenezer arrive at a mutual feeling after palling around with the film’s nazgûl-coded ghost of christmas yet to come (robert strange, cloaked in cgi), who forces the misanthrope to face the emptiness of his own miserable existence. “The flame of humanity still flickers within you,” someone tells Scrooge, but the slapstick pageantry of Depp’s performance sabotages the movie by keeping that flame at a low simmer from the start. I didn’t believe the fire had ever gone out any more than I believed that it was eventually rekindled, as this Ebenezer Scrooge is far too elastic and self-amused to convincingly suggest that he’s experiencing a permanent change of heart. He can’t even sustain a facial expression for more than a few seconds before he starts mugging around in search of another one.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there will, of course, be those who insist that i only panned “ebenezer” because johnny depp is in it, and i suppose they’re at least half-right about that, if not quite for the reason they assume. The truth is that it would be a lot more interesting and true to the spirit of Dickens’ classic if I liked this movie in spite of Depp rather than disliking it because of him, as I can’t help but share the author’s opinion that everyone is theoretically capable of redemption, be it measure by measure or miraculously complete.

Alas, the actor’s “comeback” performance is just yet another thing that he ought to be sorry for.

Paramount Pictures will release “Ebenezer” in theaters on Friday, November 13.

#111. 10 Great HBO Shows With Endings That Change Everything

📅 13 Nov 2026

10 Great HBO Shows With Endings That Change Everything

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://collider.com/best-hbo-show-finales-change-everything/

Diungkapkan bahwa the following article contains spoilers. No matter how many seasons it lasts, what themes it focuses on, or even which genre it exists within, every television series must eventually reckon with how to execute a meaningful finale. Many series opt for a cathartic wind-down, a safe and comfortable ending that offers closure to the audience. However, some series do something a little different, opting to strive for more ambitious conclusions that have a more dramatic effect on viewers.

Diungkapkan bahwa many of the series included ended with bold and brash big swings that completely reframed how viewers regarded the show. Others misfired as underwhelming resolutions to iconic titles, the backlash of which completely changed how television as a medium regards the art of delivering a climactic episode and season. All of these finales have made an undeniable impact on the format and its fans, and all stand as noteworthy chapters in HBO’s impressive and extended stay as the flagship brand of television excellence in the 21st century.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it is a conclusive shift that isn’t necessarily restricted to the series finale. After all, a tone of realism and uncertainty permeates the entire five-season run, but The Wire’s conclusion does reframe the series quite substantially. Revolving around the complex criminal ecosystem of Baltimore, spanning from the street-level drug dealers to the politics of City Hall, The Wire delivers an all-encompassing, novelistic epic of modern American crime, one laced with dozens of focal characters on both sides of the law.

Diungkapkan bahwa towards the end of the final season, it begins to become clear that creator david simon has no intention of wrapping character arcs up in a neat little bow that will give viewers a sense of closure. In the context of the series itself, it’s a thought-provoking conclusion about the nature of society and the way things both change and stay the same over time. Instead, The Wire ends as a grim meditation on the cyclical nature of organized crime, institutional corruption, and bureaucratic inefficiency. Pertaining more to television at large, however, The Wire’s resolution proved that major series don’t need to end with clarity or cliffhangers to be compelling.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the air of infamy that surrounded game of thrones thanks to its final season has begun to dissipate — the success of house of the dragon and a knight of the seven kingdoms has been influential in this — but the impact of what the epic fantasy series actually changed is still being felt. This isn’t a reference to the plotting of the story, but rather to the way television as a medium changed in the wake of Game of Thrones’ finale and the outpouring of audience disgust.

Diungkapkan bahwa it shifted the paradigm of television storytelling. Suddenly, it wasn’t enough to run with an enticing premise and figure it out on the go. Showrunners and writers had to approach major, ongoing series with a mind to how the story would end, or risk facing strong backlash from the fanbase. Granted, some major series haven’t learned the lesson in the ensuing years, and the nature of television storytelling was already evolving due to the rampant rise in streaming services, but Game of Thrones’ conclusion has proven to be a cautionary tale of negligence and subversion, with most shows since opting to conclude in a manner that honors central themes and character dynamics of their respective stories.

Sebagaimana diketahui, barry is one of those series that has come out since the fallout of game of thrones, one where the lessons hbo learned from its failure have been most evident. After four seasons following the violent hitman struggling to transition from a life of crime to a career on the stage, Barry ends with a poignant sense of inevitable tragedy that dismantles the antihero redemption trope, then closes with a 10-year time jump that sees Barry’s (Bill Hader) life being recontextualized and completely misinterpreted in an adoring Hollywood biopic.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the thematic notes that barry flaunted throughout the four seasons are beautifully handled in “wow,” which also adds a healthy dose of social commentary at the expense of glamorizing entertainment and the audiences that embrace it. The series as a whole is redefined in its final minutes, pivoting from a black comedy crime thriller to a scorching indictment of Hollywood sanitization. With every major character also facing appropriate ends to their arcs, Barry’s finale is a masterclass in how to end a story with thematic punch and emotional deftness.

Diungkapkan bahwa there have been plenty of series that have completely changed their own nature in their finale; some have even altered the fabric of television with their resolutions, but few have done what curb your enthusiasm did with its swan song outing. The hit comedy series follows the sensationalized life of Larry David, the producer of Seinfeld, as he drifts through Hollywood aimlessly. After 12 seasons and 120 episodes, it ends with Larry on trial in Atlanta, with “No Lessons Learned” delivering a meta recreation of Seinfeld’s infamous and divisive finale.

Berdasarkan laporan, it’s clever, endearing, and cathartic for all who felt undermined by seinfeld’s finale, especially as it ends on a twist that sees larry walk free, leading him and jerry seinfeld to declare that would have been a better conclusion for their hit ‘90s sitcom. It’s an admission that Seinfeld was flawed that also serves as a perfect finale for Curb Your Enthusiasm in its own right, making it possibly the only TV show ever made with a finale that has directly changed the perception of a separate series.

Sebagaimana diketahui, criminally underrated, show me a hero is a breathtaking political drama that uses the tragic true story of the youngest mayor of yonkers, new york, to explore the complexities of desegregation, the cost of political conviction, and how grassroots humanity clashes violently with institutional power. Oscar Isaac is brilliant as Nick Wasicsko, with much of the miniseries revolving around his desire to embrace a low-income housing project that many of his constituents are viciously opposed to.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the miniseries adamantly rejects the comfort of white savior heroics, delving into the grim reality of the true story that sees wasicsko grow paranoid after losing an election and eventually commit suicide. It shatters the tone of an idealistic, progressive politician navigating the red tape of city hall, highlighting Wasicsko’s egotistical knack for defining his self-worth through his career as a damning fault, while also illustrating the callous, arduous nature of true systemic change.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the leftovers is one of those series that feels like everything changes every episode. While it is a slow and meditative show, the depth it invests in its characters constantly brings new revelations to the fold, not only in their own lives as they navigate heartache, frustration, and rage, but in accordance with overarching story themes of grief, trauma, and the human condition as well. Overall, The Leftovers unfolds in a world reeling from the “Sudden Departure”, an inexplicable event in which two percent of the world’s population vanished in an instant.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the series finale, “the book of nora,” transpires years after the rest of the series, exploring an uneasy reunion between nora (carrie coon) and kevin (justin theroux). It revels in the surrealist intensity and compassionate dramatic might that defined the series at its best, ending on an unproven explanation as to what caused the Sudden Departure, then leans on empathy and choice in its final moments, rather than a traditional, plot-centered resolution. It’s a bold decision, but it perfectly suits the series’ overarching tone and brings touching closure to Kevin and Nora’s relationship.

Diungkapkan bahwa blending corporate satire with engrossing, high-stakes drama, succession fast became one of hbo’s greatest ever series in its exploration of the vying for power that erupts between three siblings when their father, the aging founder and head of a multi-billion-dollar multimedia company, signals his intent to retire. It is a manic fight for power and position with no blow being deemed below the belt, and yet the fourth and final season still ends in a manner that leaves viewers numb and shocked.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the kinship the roy siblings display as they stand against lukas matsson’s (alexander skarsgård) efforts to buy waystar royco gives way to total desperation and betrayal. It proves that the inherited wealth and influence the Roys flaunted made them incapable of ever following in their father’s footsteps, and their festering animosity with one another, as their shared childhood trauma went unresolved, was instrumental in them fragmenting and losing everything they wanted. It is quite brilliant how a series that features such unlikable and conniving characters leaves the audience feeling hollow, if not completely rattled, at their failure.

Sebagaimana diketahui, based on gillian flynn’s novel of the same name, sharp objects is a methodical, meandering crime thriller that anchors its drama in camille preaker’s (amy adams) investigation of the murder of two young girls and the inner turmoil she experiences as she returns to her hometown of wind gap and is confronted with the ghosts of her traumatic childhood. It holds a captivating Southern Gothic atmosphere, a litany of exceptional performances, and a macabre balance of character drama and murder mystery, but its greatest asset is the festering sense of dreadful unpredictability it exudes throughout the entirety of its eight-episode run.

Sebagaimana diketahui, even with viewers accustomed to its volatile plot twists, sharp objects completely changes the nature of its story in its final episode. In fact, it does so many times. The most striking of which comes in the final minute of the series, revealing a horrifying truth that shatters Camille’s sense of self-growth and safety. Accompanied by a credits sequence intercut with shots that force the audience to bask in the terrifying truth, Sharp Objects delivers an unforgettable ending that elevates it from a gripping psychological thriller to a masterclass in nightmarish suspense.

Berdasarkan laporan, six feet under is essentially a tale of mortality and the human condition wrapped up in a dark comedy about the dysfunctional fisher family and their management of a funeral home in the aftermath of their patriarch’s death. It’s funny, often poignant and sad, always thought-provoking and compelling, and it ends with what is arguably the greatest series finale in the history of television, a feat of storytelling steeped in catharsis, closure, and beautiful thematic touch.

Diungkapkan bahwa within the context of the series itself, it recalibrated all the death and drama as being a simple fact within the wonder of life, transforming the show from being an acidic satirical dramedy to a powerful ode to family and existence itself. Its flash-forward montage and evocative use of Sia’s “Breath Me” only add to the emotional resolution. Through this, Six Feet Under even redefined the commercial possibilities for television, with the episode marking a major breakthrough for Sia that proved a perfect needle-drop moment could define a series’ legacy for decades to come.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it should come as no surprise that the sopranos’ finale altered the course of television history. After all, the series itself did so from its very first episode. Whether it was through presenting such a complex and challenging antihero in Tony Soprano (James Gandolfini), pioneering long-form serialized drama on the small screen, or simply through its stronger appetite for graphic material, The Sopranos revolutionized the modern age of television drama, and its finale marks another major evolutionary step for storytelling in the medium.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it is iconic in its own right. It was divisive at the time, but it has come to be heralded as a stroke of genius. The diner, the uneasy tension, Journey’s “Don’t Stop Believin’”, and, of course, the cut to black. Almost 20 years on, people still discuss what they think happened to Tony, but from the perspective of television drama, it proved that series didn’t necessarily need to end with neat, conclusive closure to be rewarding. It proved ambiguity had a huge part to play in 21st-century television; it redefined how audiences engaged with television (especially as it coincided with the rising popularity of the internet and social media), and it remains one of the best and boldest TV finales of all time.

#112. ‘La Bola Negra’ Defied Hollywood’s Expectations—and Made Movie Stars out of Miguel Bernardeau and Guitarricadelafuente

‘La Bola Negra’ Defied Hollywood’s Expectations—and Made Movie Stars out of Miguel Bernardeau and Guitarricadelafuente

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.vanityfair.com/story/la-bola-negra

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in 1936, federico garcía lorca, the spanish poet and playwright, was working on a new play, la bola negra, which was never completed. Only four pages of it were found. Later that year, the 38-year-old homosexual anti-fascist sympathizer was executed during the Spanish Civil War on the orders of right-wing military authorities. Their glamorous but gritty film stars Spaniards Miguel Bernardeau, of Elite fame, along with Álvaro Lafuente Calvo, the singer known as Guitarricadelafuente, in his first major acting role. Ninety years later, Spanish directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi have crafted a new, ambitious film named after these scant remnants. La Bola Negra is an epic that spans close to a century; it follows several gay men whose lives are bound together by their identities, love and loss, and the looming presence of the Spanish Civil War, all under the shadow of García Lorca’s work.

Diungkapkan bahwa there are works of art that escape definitions, pieces of media that transcend. The film contains stories that speak of fear, of desire, of guilt, and of shame. La Bola Negra, both the film and the play, is a biography and a document of war; a love story and a tale of generational trauma; an examination of queerness in Spanish history. And it is a work that defies the easy summary of a logline.

Diungkapkan bahwa “so you would like us to craft that sentence for you,” bernardeau, 29, says, laughing while sitting next to guitarricadelafuente at a restaurant in manhattan. He’s athletic and handsome. He comes across as a classic macho onscreen, perhaps a residue of the characters he’s been cast as, but in person he is softer and warm, thoughtful. His hair is cut in a shaggy semi-mullet, and he’s wearing a Dolce & Gabbana black T-shirt featuring a young Monica Bellucci, a vintage find.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it’s a movie that when you finish it, it makes you want to live,” guitarricadelafuente, 29, says. Like Bernardeau, he’s disarmingly attractive, but his persona is more open. His curly hair spills over his forehead onto his wire-frame eyeglasses. As Guitarrica—a diminutive for guitar in Aragonese (his family has roots in Aragon) and his stage-name shorthand—he sings about romance and sex, mixing the sounds of Spanish tradition with the synths and reverberations of pop. Not unlike their characters, Bernardeau appears more stoic, as if he’s standing on firmer ground; Guitarrica is lighter on his feet and bashful, perhaps settling into the newness of being a movie star.

Berdasarkan laporan, “not to be dramatic,” guitarrica continues, “but people, friends that have seen the movie with us, it takes them a moment to compose themselves after,” he says. ” Bernardeau looks at his costar with admiration and utters a line from the film: “Nadie desaparece del todo” (No one disappears completely). “Like, fuck, it’s an intense film. I think it makes you want to live and not do anything half-hearted. “It’s a phrase that Rafael says that keeps coming back to me,” he says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, with the enormity of approaching garcía lorca, an idol for spaniards, a paragon for writers, and a hero for queer men, calvo and ambrossi (both modern versions of all these things) were not bold enough to attempt to complete la bola negra. Instead they built an affecting universe around it, drawing inspiration from it and other works by García Lorca, as well as co-writer Alberto Conejero’s La Piedra Oscura. The latter was itself loosely inspired by Rafael Rodríguez Rapún, a companion of García Lorca and a member of his theater troupe, who died as a soldier during the civil war.

Diungkapkan bahwa the film tells three stories: that of sebastián (guitarrica) in 1937, a young trumpeter taken into the nationalist army who encounters rafael (bernardeau) as a new prisoner put under his watch; of carlos (milo quifes) in 1932, the lead character in garcía lorca’s original play and a young gay man who is denied membership to a casino club because of his sexuality; and in 2017, of alberto (carlos gonzález), a modern-day historian who, following the death of his grandfather and an excavation into his past, finds himself indelibly connected to the other men. In Carlos’s vignette, club members vote on his admission using black and white balls, where a black ball (la bola negra) signifies a negative. When Carlos receives several, he has to confront his father. The tension between shame and confession becomes the heart of the film.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sebastián is a character who is, as guitarrica puts it, “like a custom-made suit” for him. He ran into Ambrossi and Calvo after performing at the Primavera Sound festival in Barcelona two years ago. Instead they told him they were writing a film with Conejero, and offered him the role of Sebastián. “I thought they’d ask me to make a song for the soundtrack,” he says. “It was one of those nights where, after a few drinks, you kind of forget what was said,” he says with a laugh. “I wasn’t confident at all, nothing was clear,” Guitarrica says, “but I saw the faith they had in me. But he heard from Calvo after that, and soon he was in Madrid meeting with the directors. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa bernardeau, who was invited to audition for rafael, also had his doubts. “I didn’t think I did well,” Bernardeau says of his audition. ” But after a week and a half of self-inflicted torture, he was asked to read with Guitarrica and was then offered the role. “I was like damn, I missed the opportunity of a lifetime. He was sure about his costar: “The choice of Álvaro made perfect sense,” he says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, bernardeau and guitarrica were familiar with each other’s work. “But we met as Sebastián and Rafael,” Bernardeau says. These days they appear to have the kind of friendship, of reverence for each other, of two men who’ve gone to war together—even if just on camera.

Berdasarkan laporan, despite its hefty emotional punch and astonishing staging, la bola negra is a film about war. Human stories are its spoils, and the unrealized potential of lost lives is buried on the battlefields. The Spanish Civil War still looms darkly over the country. Their dead, from unknown soldiers to acclaimed names like García Lorca, have become Spain’s ghosts.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i felt a ton of responsibility,” bernardeau says of playing rafael, with his connection to a real person. (Ambrossi and Calvo gave him a reading list, and Bernardeau got to work. “There is a responsibility in telling the story of someone who is no longer here,” he says. ” Bernardeau knew of García Lorca much like anyone who learns about their home country’s foremost literary giants in school, but the life of Rafael perhaps eluded the textbooks. “By making this film, I found that he is important to many people, and I didn’t know that. ).

Diungkapkan bahwa for guitarrica, the process was more internal. The character of Sebastián was crafted for him, which afforded him the license to find himself in the role, he says, and consider history by imagining what it would have been like to have lived it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “there was a lot of introspection,” he says. Acting, Guitarrica has found, means excavating old wounds. Did he encounter any turmoil? “Well, yes,” he laughs, “but I’m not telling you about that. Back in Madrid, during that first meeting with the directors, they asked him if he had any emotional traumas. Guitarrica was also learning how to arrive at certain emotions “and unearth my own experiences to be able to give nuance to my character,” he says. “I said no, and they said, we’ll see,” he says, laughing. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, since the film premiered at the cannes film festival in may and received a 20-minute standing ovation, with ambrossi and calvo winning the award for best direction (alongside fatherland director pawel pawlikowski), bernardeau and guitarrica have covered magazines in spain and beyond and become two of the internet’s latest fixations. La Bola Negra will also represent Spain in the best international feature film category at the Academy Awards, should it be nominated.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i love that it’s a story that we feel is so ours, that is such a fundamental part of our society and our collective imagination,” bernardeau says. “The war has impacted us through generations, and it is part of us in different ways. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa he says he doesn’t want to romanticize, but the global reception of such a regional story has given him some faith in humanity. “Because, in the end, it shows that we’re all different, but all the same; that the most personal is also the most creative,” he says, making sure I know that he’s quoting a phrase attributed to Martin Scorsese.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i think that this film is largely about an idea that is pretty straightforward,” guitarrica says. And that is a very universal story. “Simply, it’s about the drive to live. Of not leaving anything on the table or unfinished. ”.

#113. Rings Of Power Season 3 Features The Most Gruesome TV Scene Of 2026

Rings Of Power Season 3 Features The Most Gruesome TV Scene Of 2026

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the land of mordor is where the shadows lie, and this article is where major spoilers lie. Read no further if you haven't watched the Season 3 premiere episodes of "The Rings of Power. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the rings of power" is a tragedy. As far as prequels go, this one is not as full of doom and gloom as "Andor" — a show where audiences knew the main character was destined to die tragically — but it is still a show all about the rise of an evil that almost conquered Middle-earth. Indeed, though there are some surprising main characters in Season 3, the true star of "Rings of Power" is the Dark Lord Sauron (Charlie Vickers), who spends each season lying and manipulating his way to ruining everyone else's day.

Diungkapkan bahwa this was especially prominent than in season 2, which was all about sauron making the elves believe he was an envoy of the valar so that they'd help him make the titular rings of power. In particular, Sauron spent the entire season gaslighting the show's best and most tragic character, Celebrimbor (Charles Edwards). Episode after episode, Sauron used Celebrimbor's vanity and pride to his advantage, scheming and lying into making Celebrimbor his friend and ally, before stabbing him in the chest with a pike.

Diungkapkan bahwa this leads to "rings of power" season 3 featuring the most gruesome tv scene of 2026. When Sauron returns to his little office in Barad-dûr after failing to make the One Ring yet again, the Dark Lord gets a visit from the ghost of Celebrimbor, who mocks Sauron's failures at trying to replicate the dead elven smith's work.

And right there, in front of Sauron, is the rotting body of Celebrimbor, hanging on a wall like a trophy.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what makes this horrifying is not only that sauron still keeps the dead body of celebrimbor around, but the fact that it's a rotting mess with arrows sticking out of the torso. Making matters worse, Skelebrimbor is hung from a wall like a war banner.

Berdasarkan laporan, this, of course, is a reference to the actual books. Tolkien himself wrote, Celebrimbor's dead body was "hung upon a pole, shot through with Orc-arrows" and turned upon Elrond's forces like a banner for Sauron's army. It's why fans affectionately refer to this act as "Celebrimbanner. R. R. As J. " It is arguably one of the cruelest things the Dark Lord ever did — which is saying something considering the untold number of people that died because of him.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, seeing the body of celebrimbor hanging on a wall — the flesh rotting away, an expression of fear and shock on the skeleton — is horrifying, and easily the most gruesome piece of imagery in the entire "lord of the rings" franchise. There is no reason why Sauron needs to have kept the body of Celebrimbor, other than to assert his cruelty.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, and yet, it leads to a rather hilarious scene of the ghost of celebrimbor appearing only to taunt sauron, ragebaiting the dark lord and mocking his inability to craft anything as majestic as the great smith celebrimbor. He even tells Sauron that his orcs now pity him because of how pathetic his jewelry crafting skills are. It's a testament to Charlie Vickers for the subtle ways in which you can tell the insults are actually getting at Sauron. Meanwhile Charles Edwards reminds us why he is one of the best pieces of casting in this show, with this short but impactful scene in a third season that otherwise struggles to live up to hype.

#116. Steam’s Angriest New Game Is the Perfect Place to Channel Your AI Hate

📅 13 Nov 2026

Steam’s Angriest New Game Is the Perfect Place to Channel Your AI Hate

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/virtue-and-a-sledgehammer-review/

Virtue and a Sledgehammer rages against AI and finds peace in grief.

Virtue and a Sledgehammer rages against AI and finds peace in grief.

Diungkapkan bahwa there are plenty of good reasons to have an adversarial relationship with generative ai. You could go to war over the tech’s environmental impact, its catastrophic impact on labor, the way it has driven up the cost of RAM, or the fact that it’s an empire built on mass theft. But there’s also the existential horror of it all. Imagine what a world where human beings forfeit all of their brainpower to machines would look like. Where nobody can be bothered to write so much as an email to one another. Where photos are replaced with digital approximations of cherished moments. Where art is no longer created by people who have something to express, but by those who only see it as a space-filling product.

Berdasarkan laporan, the greater threat of an unchecked ai industry is that it will siphon the soul out of humanity. And what are we without that?.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s a question that haunts pratelle, the tortured star of deconstructeam and selkie harbour’s rage-filled virtue and a sledgehammer. Generative AI is a clear target in this vital and timely story about resisting harmful technology before it's too late, but that’s only one piece of the game’s more thoughtful meditation on what makes a person human, and why we must accept our limitations as a species. Grief crosses paths with cultural frustration as Pratelle sets out on a quest to smash a town full of bots. That even means finding peace with death.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, reeling from the loss of her mother, pratelle returns to her hometown — with a sledgehammer in tow — to discover that everyone’s consciousness has been transferred into walking machines. Scattered flashbacks gradually reveal that her sister, Nina, is behind the town’s transformation into a robotic paradise. Unable to process the impending death of her mother, Nina becomes obsessed with the idea of saving her mom by letting her thoughts live on in a machine body. Pratelle detests the idea, and eventually returns home with the intention of destroying her sister’s work.

Berdasarkan laporan, pratelle’s rage manifests in a simple but effective mechanic: she can smash every bot and building in sight with a sledgehammer. And holding it as long as she can results in a Hulk-like smash that can level an entire house. Tapping the button simply lets her shove bots away. Holding the button down allows her to swing it. It’s a one-note bit of gameplay, but it’s as much as the three-hour story calls for. There’s an undeniable power that comes from pounding a bot into oblivion. Visceral sound design emphasizes the impact of each swing as walls crumble in an ear-splitting stone downpour.

Sebagaimana diketahui, virtue and sledgehammer’s stance on ai isn’t subtle, nor is it trying to be. The entire premise of the game even evokes Ridley Scott’s iconic 1984-referencing Apple commercial, where a runner dressed in red throws a sledgehammer through a screen as Big Brother speaks to the brainwashed masses. It sees an impending dystopia and wishes one person could have the power to cut it off at the knees. (It’s a reclamation of the image in some way, given that an Apple is now a very major player in the tech climate that Virtue and a Sledgehammer is so ready to topple. It’s an aggressive rejection of the tech built for anyone who has ever said what they wish they could do to a data center, out of earshot of a cellphone microphone. ).

Virtue and a Sledgehammer frames the idea of letting go as the kindest thing you can do for a person.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but catharsis is only a temporary bliss; virtue and sledgehammer is much more about the problems that can’t be solved with destruction. Once her mother’s brain stops functioning, she will no longer exist. Pratelle faces reality in a coldly blunt manner. A body is just a body, in her mind; it’s your thoughts that make you who you are. Nina refuses to accept that, and it’s what leads her to believe that a person could live forever if they give themself over to a tech singularity. Death is death. The real heart of the story comes from Pratelle and Nina’s divergent responses to an inevitable death. And if you could transplant those thoughts into a bot and simulate consciousness, isn’t that the same thing as being alive?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, virtue and sledgehammer wades into similar territory explored by yorgos lanthimos’ alps. The idea is that it could allow people to wean themselves into acceptance by giving them a substitute to fill that sudden void in their life. Is that ethical, or a manipulative business practice that causes more harm than good? It’s a Lanthimos movie, so you can probably guess the answer if you’re familiar with the pitch-black filmmaker. The Greek film centers around a service that helps people get over a recent death in their life by sending them an actor who impersonates the deceased. But Virtue and a Sledgehammer approaches similar questions, tied up in an AI premise that’s beginning to feel less sci-fi by the day, with a genuine philosophical curiosity.

Berdasarkan laporan, while destroying everything in a blind rage, pratelle is challenged by the horrifying idea that nina could be right. Her empathy is repeatedly tested by cowering robots who beg not to be killed, as is yours when you’re left deciding whether to hear their pleas or treat them as the cold ramblings of a machine. After all, the robots she’s crushing house the thoughts and feelings of real people she once knew. It would all be easier for everyone involved if you could accept the comforting idea that immortality is possible.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but it’s not. We are flawed creatures with bodies and minds that are built to break down. It’s not a scientific problem to be solved. You can skip the funerals to avoid staring at that cold truth lying in an open casket, but that doesn’t reverse a loss. Virtue and a Sledgehammer isn’t trying to bum players out with a bleak reality. One of the great pains of living is knowing that everyone you’ve ever met will someday die. Instead, it embraces the fact that this cycle of life, death, grief, and acceptance is an inseparable piece of our humanity. What makes humans special is that we aren’t machines that operate with 100% efficiency. The fact that we know that and still continue on, trying to forge legacies and leave the world a better place than we found it, is remarkable. And it’s remarkable because we know how fragile and impermanent we are, not in spite of it.

Diungkapkan bahwa virtue and a sledgehammer frames the idea of letting go as the kindest thing you can do for a person. It’s an acknowledgment of an irreplaceable humanity that can only come from an imperfectly designed being. That’s something that a tech industry so overeager to push humanity past its natural limits fails to grasp. Let us fail, let us grow, and let us die. The absence is an invisible monument to their life; it is not a void to be filled with a substitution. Otherwise, what’s the point of living?.

Meanwhile, quite a few folks received Additional Literary Material credits (which will not be seen on screen). Berdasarkan laporan, my greatest fear regarding "avengers: doomsday" is that it'll be undone by superhero clutter. Diungkapkan bahwa i've been encouraged by some of what i've heard over the last month – in particular, that james marsden's cyclops plays a significant role in the film. Gunn's "Superman" caught on because it foregrounded hope in a thoughtful, non-anodyne way. I really don't want a relentlessly dour "Avengers: Doomsday," which is the vibe I'm getting from the pea green aesthetic of the trailers (and its fast food tie-ins). I'm not sure AI-friendly filmmakers like the Russos should be in charge of a franchise that, overall, appeals to our sense of humanity. We live in bleak times. #120. Sandra Wollner’s ‘Everytime’ Is a Stunning Film About Grief Like You’ve Never Seen Before

📅 11 Nov 2026

Sandra Wollner’s ‘Everytime’ Is a Stunning Film About Grief Like You’ve Never Seen Before

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.indiewire.com/awards/consider-this/sandra-wollner-everytime-grief-video-games-fall-1235226504/

Sebagaimana diketahui, few human emotions are as fathomable as grief. Someone (or something) was here, had meaning and value and presence, and is now gone. The pain that accompanies that void may manifest in different people in different ways, but its very existence is understandable. There is a hole, a gap, an empty space. What makes people happy? What makes them sad? What makes them angry? Grief, well, that’s an easier question with a tougher answer.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for her third feature film, german filmmaker sandra wollner tackles the most tangible of dramatic genres — the grief tale — and turns it on its head in a way that our own david ehrlich called “infinitely beguiling. ” Mostly, the film shows how infinitely elastic and malleable this genre is, and the emotions that power it. Related Stories Jensen Huang’s Biopic Feels Inevitable — The Right One Might Be Impossible Miles Teller Opens Up About ‘Paper Tiger,’ Adam Driver, and Losing His Home Before Filming James Gray’s Movie.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the logline for the un certain regard winner is simple enough: after the death of teenager jessie (carla hüttermann), her mother ella (birgit minichmayr), her little sister melli (lotte shirin keiling), and her boyfriend lux (tristán lópez) form an unlikely family unit as they attempt to move on. To say much else is spoiler-y in the truest of senses: It would detract from the joy and wonder of watching this story unfold.

That Wollner’s film is doing something different with seemingly well-trod material is obvious from the start, as “Everytime” layers on cut scenes from the video game “Vintage Story” — not “Minecraft,” though Wollner understands why the audience might think it’s the more well-known game — long before the real drama kicks in.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a familiarity with “vintage story” is not required to understand her film, wollner promised during a recent interview with indiewire. “Maybe if someone hears the dialogue of Melli and Lux, then maybe they would feel they have to know more about it, because they’re talking about how you can basically cut trees to harvest stuff and to get that, but I don’t feel that you have to know anything,” she said.

Diungkapkan bahwa wollner herself isn’t even a “hardcore gamer,” but she admires video games for their world-building and how they can encourage exploration. “It felt like the ‘Backrooms’ phenomenon, but before the ‘Backrooms’ phenomenon,” she said. And the sounds; a very ambient sound feels eerie and soothing at the same time. Her early forays into both “Vintage Story” and “Minecraft” tickled that. I was just very compelled and inspired by that. “You’re walking through infinite worlds that feel so big, but minimalistic in a way. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the idea that jessie would leave behind her own video game world that melli could then play in was one of the film’s first seeds. “[We have this] whole world of avatars and gaming communities where people meet online and then if someone really goes out, their avatar might live forever in there and create a life on its own in a way. “I thought, it’s a way of a memorial I haven’t seen so far,” she said. I just found that very intriguing, and this is why I wanted in there. ”.

While the film is unique in how it handles digital mementos — avatars, literally — Wollner also pays close attention to real-world details that can make grief feel even bigger.

Diungkapkan bahwa “one of the first scenes [i thought of] was ella lying down on the couch and hearing how her daughter would come back [into their apartment],” the filmmaker said. For example, when I was a kid, my aunt would always run down the stairs [in the apartment complex where we lived], and I would always hear her in the morning, running down in the morning. I didn’t want it to be full on, but to let us think, it couldn’t be Jessie. “It’s something I think also everybody can relate to, even with a more natural loss and not such a tragic one. The noise was very specific to this person. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, wollner was also intrigued early on by the “constellation of people” impacted by the loss of one. She needs him to grieve. But there is a big conflict in there. He needs her to forgive. “They seemed very clear to me. Of course, I could have made this conflict much bigger, but I really was interested in ordinary people who just try to do the right thing and just try to go along with that. They are having a weird dependent relationship. Three people who, especially the mother and the boy, really tried to do the right thing in a way. “The boy, the little girl, and the mother, it’s people I’ve met in my life in several decades, I would say, variations of them, but somehow similar constellations,” she said. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, having her own child added a new dimension to the film, even for wollner. The filmmaker was editing the film when her daughter was born (her longtime partner is writer and cinematographer Timm Kröger, who also worked on the digital imaging in “Everytime”), an experience that deepened her understanding of her own work.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the film’s second half, the trio travel to tenerife, spain on holiday, a place that baby jessie (who we’ve seen in home videos) once visited. There, they discover another baby, who looks just like Jessie, playing happily in the same quiet space that baby Jessie once occupied.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we watched the scene again of baby jessie sitting there, and we looked at each other,” she said. And I felt, oh, I really nailed it! I mean, that sounds so stupid, but when I had the baby, I think, as many people feel, you still sometimes have the feeling, oh, where does it come from? It’s suddenly here. “I always understood what [that scene] means for me, but there, we really felt it for the first time, being a parent. Suddenly there’s a person there. It’s like with that moment when she walks around the corner, and baby’s sitting there. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, wollner was also compelled by the way we memorize different places and the unpredictability of memory. The odd little space, located in the far reaches of the resort’s clubhouse, comes to haunt Ella, Melli, and Lux in different ways, forever linked to Jessie and her absence.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “when my dad died, i was with him, and i suddenly had this image of him standing somewhere in this bend on the river and fishing, and it felt so familiar,” the filmmaker said. And this is the thing that then comes back. Sometimes we can make them happen to come. We cannot control when we get a memory. It’s this weird banal little room with this weird banal kitschy toy that is playing this music. But we never know if maybe the weird place where we saw our baby sitting or the weird moment is the one that haunts us the most. “This memory intruded on my present. They’re just coming. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, those “banal little” details pack immense emotional power. So do turns from Minichmayr and López, who never turn to over-the-top histrionics to convey their grief. Wollner’s choice to set the majority of the film a year after Jessie’s death helped, giving the characters some distance from the immediate stab of loss.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “it was a conscious choice to pick some time after the death [to mostly focus the film on],” she said. Maybe you can be angry again, then you accept. It’s just this messy thing that you can feel for a very long time. That just felt too overwhelming. And sometimes we are made to believe that grief comes in these neat boxes to check: Now you’re sad, now you’re angry, now you accept. “As a writer, we need to know what happened in the time between, and so I wrote that as well, but it honestly felt not depictable. I wasn’t interested in these big emotions. I feel I can only fail to show that. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa keiling also offers a nuanced performance, built more on a kid’s curiosity than on saddling the young actress with big, showy scenes. There’s no screaming and crying here, no sobbing or yelling. But that doesn’t mean that Keiling wasn’t accessing some major emotions.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i love to work with kids,” wollner said. I just fell in love and thought, oh, she’s exactly what I thought of Melli could be and even better, so I trusted the script to her. “And even having a kid, I think I still am a kid in a way. For this one, I met Lotte, I had not met another kid, I only met her, I did not do any other castings. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, wollner worked with fellow filmmaker juli neuhaus, who served as a “kids’ coach” for the younger members of the cast. Wollner and Neuhaus were eager to meet Keiling where she was. The young performer loves to draw, so she would draw the scenes before performing them, to better understand what they were about, which allowed her to access a full spectrum of feeling.

Diungkapkan bahwa “with melli, there was no scene where she really had to act her grief,” she said. It was really playful. So, actually for her, it was, I would say, like a very light shoot. Playful. “I always felt that the film itself, the editing and the framing, the absence, we see her doing her homework, and then we see the same room behind her, but now we know that the sister is not there anymore, I always felt that this will tell us the grief, so she doesn’t need to act it. She doesn’t need to feel the heavy weight of that. If she holds her phone and is texting her sister, it will already make us feel the grief. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, still, for all its sense of fantasy and play, “everytime” is about a terrible heartbreak. We can do nothing about it. Yet, as ever, Wollner chose to depict Jessie’s sudden, shocking death in a unique way, tracking her fall from a tall building while out with Lux from a great distance away. We can see it. That’s grief, too.

“This was one that really was clear to me in the writing process already, that we’re going to have this lens and that we have this weird perspective of the universe itself looking at it, being so far away and still not able to do something about it, but still witnessing so intimate,” she said.

Diungkapkan bahwa the actors were on one high-rise building, while wollner and her crew were on another, about half a mile away. I had a 3,000-millimeter consumer camera, which is an insane lens,” she said. It feels really not OK. “And we had this insane lens. But I was sure that I wanted to work with exactly that length or something similar to that, that feels kind of forbidden to be so close and too far away at the same time. “It’s really like you don’t want to point it on people. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, while the scene is shot as if jessie and lux are very close to the edge of the building, the actors were not. (Hüttermann later told Wollner that she still had the feeling she might fall, even with myriad safety measures in place. That’s just how immersive the entire thing felt. ) Hüttermann’s actual fall was shot in a studio, and their visual effects supervisor Kariem Saleh combined that footage with the outdoor shots.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, because they needed a certain kind of light, wollner estimated they had only about five takes to get it right, though she knew they would likely only get one shot with the “perfect” light. Her script also called for the camera to follow a bird after the fall, but she said with a laugh, “Unfortunately, no bird came in exactly that moment. ” (They lensed other birds, though, and those also ended up in the final composite shot. ).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we worked so many hours just on the sounds, just to get the right level of there is a little sound, and there is a little tink when she falls down, a little bit,” she said. I mean, it’s weird to say that, but I was happy, but I felt the first time that it actually worked. “Just to realize, given how far away we had to be, how does the sound have to be? We worked the whole time on that, and I never really felt it until I sat at Cannes in the audience. And I heard the gasps for the first time and really it went through my bones. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, wollner remains very emotionally connected to the film, constantly talking about the way certain scenes make her feel, either while making them or editing them or even seeing them with an audience. Since Cannes, audiences have been talking about its genuinely thrilling third act and the implications of its final scenes. Of course, such a deep-feeling filmmaker crafted such a beguiling film, one that invites all sorts of responses and theories. And while we won’t spoil them here, we had to ask: What did Wollner want her viewers to feel in those moments?.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the feeling that i wanted to have is that [this film that is] grounded or hopefully grounded in the beginning, then suddenly you walk around the corner and you feel still some ground, but it’s such an odd place now and you don’t know,” she said. That was clear from the beginning. “I always hoped it doesn’t feel just dreamy, but there is some groundedness to it and that the people still react in a way that made sense for them, the characters, but that you don’t know what room you entered now, some kind of back room. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, and, as fantastical as it might sound, she’s clear: it’s all real. “I mean, it’s such a cliché to say that, but everything we see at the end is true at the same time,” she said.

A 1-2 Special release, the film is in limited theaters now, with a wide release to come in February 2027.

#121. 5 Miniseries From The 1970s Better Than Any Modern Show

📅 13 Nov 2026

5 Miniseries From The 1970s Better Than Any Modern Show

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/1970s-tv-miniseries-better-than-shows-today/

Berdasarkan laporan, every decade has had great miniseries, and in the 1970s, there were notable miniseries that still hold up, being better than any modern tv show. The list of the best TV shows of all time includes shows from different decades, including some from the 1970s. That decade left a cultural stamp across different areas, and on TV, it brought now-classics like M*A*S*H, Columbo, Happy Days, and All in the Family.

Berdasarkan laporan, most of the best tv shows from the 1970s have various seasons, but this decade also produced some of the most notable miniseries of all time. Miniseries are especially appealing as they tell a complete story in a limited number of episodes, which also makes them a lot easier to watch (and, in the current streaming era, they are easy to binge-watch). A lot can be said about an era through the most notable miniseries released in every decade, and those from the 1970s are no exception.

Berdasarkan laporan, the best miniseries from the 1970s reflect historical trauma, changes in traditional domestic life, explore corruption and decay, and question morals and traditions of the time that had been carried for years. Many of them made TV history thanks to their themes, production value, and stories, and even more impressive is that they have aged so well that they are better than any modern show.

Sebagaimana diketahui, based on robert graves’ novels i, claudius and claudius the god, i, claudius is an epic drama produced by bbc television and aired in 1976. I, Claudius takes the audience all the way back to the early Roman Empire to explore the rise and fall of Roman Emperor Claudius (Derek Jacobi), from the reign of Augustus (Brian Blessed), the first Emperor of Rome, to the many betrayals that lead to his downfall and the ascent of his stepson, Nero (Christopher Biggins). Also part of the cast of I, Claudius are John Hurt, Patricia Quinn, John Rhys-Davies, and Patrick Stewart.

Diungkapkan bahwa although i, claudius initially got a negative reception, it went on to become a huge success, earning different awards and now being regarded as one of the best british tv shows of all time. I, Claudius has been endlessly praised for its writing, performances (particularly that of Jacobi), and blend of political and family drama, with many critics citing it as the tonal blueprint for shows like The Sopranos and House of Cards.

Surely, some elements, like its makeup and some costumes, have been pointed out as not aging well, but that becomes a minor “problem” compared to the greatness of the rest of the show.

Diungkapkan bahwa scenes from a marriage (original title: scener ur ett äktenskap) is a swedish drama miniseries written and directed by ingmar bergman. Scenes from a Marriage focuses on divorce lawyer Marianne (Liv Ullmann) and a reader in psychology, Johan (Erland Josephson), a married couple who have renewed their marriage contract after their 10th anniversary. Marianne and Johan seem like an ideal couple and family with their two daughters, but, in reality, their marriage is crumbling.

Berdasarkan laporan, kicking off with an interview for a magazine on love, scenes from a marriage explores the disintegration of marianne and johan’s relationship over the course of a decade, all this in just six episodes. Scenes from a Marriage is one of the most influential TV shows of all time, with its biggest strengths being its dialogue, structure, performances, direction, realism, and depiction of human emotion and depth.

All episodes of Scenes from a Marriage were condensed into a theatrical version that became an international hit.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, scenes from a marriage wasn’t safe from controversy, being blamed for a rise in divorce rates in europe. Still, Scenes from a Marriage became the blueprint for modern dramas, and in 2021, it got an English-language remake starring Oscar Isaac and Jessica Chastain.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, based on john le carré’s 1974 novel of the same name, tinker tailor soldier spy is a spy drama tv series produced by the bbc and aired in 1979. Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy introduces the audience to George Smiley (Alec Guinness), deputy to the head of the British Secret Intelligence Service, known as the “Circus”, who is forced into retirement after a failed spy mission in Czechoslovakia. Smiley’s boss and head of the Circus, Control (Alexander Knox), believes there’s a mole among them, but no one believes him.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when the new leadership takes over, smiley is brought out of retirement to investigate and find the mole. Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy was a huge hit, being nominated for different awards and praised for its performances (especially that of Guinness), adaptation of Le Carré’s work, tone, pace, and overall production value, with every episode being a delightful event. Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy redefined spies on TV by portraying them as more cerebral and calculating instead of relying on gadgets and action sequences.

Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy got a sequel in 1982, titled Smiley’s People, once again starring Guinness as Smiley, but it didn’t match the success and impact of the first show.

Berdasarkan laporan, created by gerald green, holocaust: the story of the family weiss aired on nbc in 1978, and it’s told in four parts. Holocaust tells the story of the (fictional) Jewish family of Dr. Josef Weiss (Fritz Weaver), his wife Berta (Rosemary Harris), their children Karl (James Woods), Rudi (Joseph Bottoms), and Anna (Blanche Baker), along with Karl’s wife, Inga (Meryl Streep), who is a Christian, and Erik Dorf (Michael Moriarty), a lawyer who becomes a Nazi and war criminal.

Diungkapkan bahwa the first part, “the gathering darkness”, covers the beginning of dorf’s work with the ss, kristallnacht, dr. Weiss’ deportation to Poland, and Berta and the children hiding with Inga’s family, who are Nazi supporters. Part 2, “The Road to Babi Yar”, sees Berta being taken to the Warsaw Ghetto, the Babi Yar massacre, and the planning of the “Final Solution”, which is also the title of part 3, covering the construction of the death camps.

Sebagaimana diketahui, part 4, “the saving remnant”, shows the fate of the weiss family, inga, and dorf, as some are sent to auschwitz and dorf is tried for war crimes. Holocaust isn’t an easy watch, but it stands out for its performances and its more human and emotional approach to this difficult topic rather than focusing on statistics. However, Holocaust was also heavily criticized for its historical inaccuracy and one-dimensional characters, but its impact and legacy are undeniable.

Sebagaimana diketahui, based on alex haley’s 1976 novel roots: the saga of an american family, roots is a drama miniseries that explores the era of enslavement in the united states and its aftermath. For that, Roots tells the story of a family through generations, starting in the mid-1700s, with 15-year-old Kunta Kinte being captured by slave traders in West Africa and taken to America, and following his descendants all the way to after the Civil War.

Sebagaimana diketahui, roots is widely regarded as one of the best miniseries of all time, and its finale broke records, becoming the third-most-watched series finale in american tv history. Roots stood out for its narrative structure, cast, approach to complex and serious topics like slavery and racism, and overall production value. Few TV shows have had the impact that Roots had, and after all these years, it still stands as one of the best TV shows of all time.

Beau Jessup, the only child of British actress Lisa Maxwell and her husband Paul Jessup, died at the age of 27 while studying journalism at Columbia University in New York, according to her school.

Lisa Maxwell’s family is grieving a tragic loss.

Beau Jessup—the daughter of the British TV actress and her husband Paul Jessup—died at the age of 27, according to Columbia Journalism School, where Jessup was studying as a graduate student.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “columbia journalism school mourns the loss of beau jessup, a student in our m. 9 statement. program,” the school shared in a Nov. S. “We extend our deepest condolences to her family, friends, classmates and all who knew and loved her. ”.

Before her death, Jessup gave an interview with her college paper Columbia News in which she detailed how Maxwell—known for her role as Samantha Nixon on The Bill from 2001 to 2009 and as a presenter on the chat show Loose Women—inspired her to pursue journalism.

Diungkapkan bahwa “as the daughter of a television actress, i grew up with an unusual awareness of the distance between people’s lives and the stories told about them,” she shared in the interview published nov. “I saw how journalism could illuminate someone’s experiences, but also how those experiences could be distorted, simplified, or transformed into a public narrative over which the subject had very little control. 9. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, she added, “i was curious, from quite a young age, about who gets to tell people’s stories, and what happens when those stories enter the public domain. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, plus, jessup—who previously earned a master’s degree in writing for performance at the university of cambridge—used her life’s experiences to understand “the power and the responsibility of storytelling. ”.

As for what she planned to do upon graduating in May?.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i want to work as a journalist and writer, reporting on people, culture, and social questions with the rigor i’m learning at columbia,” jessup said. “I’m particularly drawn to journalism for its power and immediacy, while continuing to write for theater when a subject benefits from being explored through a different form. ”.

Jessup was also interested in continuing her creative writing, hoping to have her work reach new heights.

Diungkapkan bahwa “while completing my master’s in writing for performance at the university of cambridge, i wrote my first play, the sandbag,” she added. Geographically speaking, at least. “If I can arrange a table reading of The Sandbag in Pulitzer Hall [on campus], I’ll technically be able to claim my first play was performed on Broadway. ”.

As for Maxwell—who also voiced Kira in Jim Henson and Frank Oz’s 1982 hit movie The Dark Crystal—her career turned to soap operas after she left The Bill in 2009, as she went on to star in Hollyoaks from 2016 to 2017.
